issues.problem: [NEW, replaces the cycle-1 mushroom] The late cloud is a detached, near-black 'cannonball' floating in empty sky from 2 s on. Nothing links it to the ground. It SHRINKS between 1 s and 4 s (about 470 px to 220 px wide at the same framing) and never greys or thins. At 60 s it turns into a rigid tilted rugby ball with brushed, hairy edges and a smooth black-to-tan gradient. Ref a/c and the dossier describe a lumpy black puff that goes grey-brown, grows as it rises (about 130 m at 30 s, 150 m cap diameter by 2 min) and stays visibly attached to a dirty trail for the first seconds. At 60 s the render is about 31 m wide, 3x too narrow. Causes: (1) _column_head takes `grow` from the CURRENT column_height, so when col_fall (0.8 s) collapses the crown, r = cap*(0.35+0.65*grow) falls to about 0.5x. (2) head_color_late [0.20,0.18,0.16] with whiten_s 60 plus SOOT albedo 0.05 means even the sunlit side renders black. (3) cap_fade 70 gives no dilution. (4) The shader shear p.xz -= wind*age*pow(p.y/wind_h,1.7) is applied inside the compact puff (local slope about 1.3 at 60 s), which tilts it and streaks the noise.
issues.fix: explosion_profile.gd _column_head: compute grow from the un-collapsed height (a column_height variant without the col_fall factor, or a running max) so the head never shrinks. Use the same peak value in the density clamp. bomb_profiles mk82: cap_late_grow 2.5->5.0 (r about 45 m at 60 s, matching a thermal r about 0.25 z), head_density 0.75->0.45 with extra dilution dens *= pow(r0/r,1.5), head_color_early SOOT->[0.09,0.085,0.08], head_color_late ->[0.38,0.34,0.30], whiten_s 60->15, cap_fade 70->40. explosion_volume.gdshader: give the head a rigid drift (evaluate the shear term at head.y, not p.y: p_head.xz -= wind.xz*age*pow(clamp(head.y/wind_h,0,1.5),1.7)) and keep the per-height shear only for stem and skirt. Keep a thin, wide, low-density dirty trail (stem remnant, density 0.15, radius about 8 m) from the crater to the puff until about 10 s.

issues.problem: [NEW] The crown renders as a flat-topped inverted frustum (a flower pot or bucket) about 2.5:1 wide-to-tall. It is a uniform opaque brown-black with horizontal striations, hairy horizontally brushed 'wings' at 0.06 s, a perfectly straight horizontal top edge at 0.15-1 s, and a thin vertical seam or sliver on the axis (visible at 0.06/0.15/0.4 s and on the skirt at 8-30 s). At 2-4 s it collapses into a flat dark slab with a flat top. Ref a/c show a V-fan of 6-12 separate spiky jets with tips at different heights, grey-white puffs inside, sky between the jets and clods at the tips, about 1.3:1 (35 x 25 m). Causes: col_cone 5 makes the top 6x the base radius. In stem_density, the y-fade smoothstep(stem.y + r*0.3, ...) and the sdf_stem cap plane dv = p.y - stem.y cut every jet at the same height. The jet term nbl(vec3(ang*2.2+seed, h01*0.9, ...)) has no radial component (pure radial streaks read as horizontal brush strokes side-on), and atan(p.z,p.x) wraps at +/-pi, which produces the vertical seam.
issues.fix: bomb_profiles mk82: col_cone 5.0->2.0, col_flare 1.6->1.2, col_density 1.3->1.0. explosion_volume.gdshader stem_density: (a) sample the jet noise on periodic coordinates, e.g. nbl(vec3(cos(ang)*1.6+seed, sin(ang)*1.6, h01*0.9 + rxz/r*0.6)), with no raw atan in the lookup; (b) make coverage sparse: jet = smoothstep(0.55,0.8,jet), dens *= mix(0.08,1.4,jet), so gaps show sky and fireball; (c) give each jet its own top: top_j = stem.y*(0.55+0.6*jet), replacing both the dv plane and the y-fade with smoothstep(top_j + r*0.2, top_j - r*0.8, p.y); (d) tilt jets outward (offset p.xz by -dir*(p.y*0.35*jet)). Colour: blend stem_color toward [0.17,0.16,0.15] charcoal and add light-grey puffs (c_stem *= 1.0 + 1.2*smoothstep(0.7,0.9,sn)). Debris launch azimuths should follow the jet maxima.

At 2 s it has dragged the flame up with it, leaving a clear-sky gap under the burning ball. From 4 to 30 s a black ball floats one diameter above a separate, flat-topped dust chimney. The causes: rise_k=130 puts head_center_y at 37+130*sqrt(t), about 405 m at 8 s, roughly 4x too high. _conventional_fireball lerps the flame centre toward head_center_y by smoothstep(life*0.7), which is 62% at 2 s. head_state makes the head appear at 0.15*dur = 0.36 s. The stem rises at stem_speed_rel 0.8 x 23.6 m/s and lags behind the head.
issues.fix: Set rise_k 130 -> ~35 and rise_delay ~2.0 s, so the head centre is ~60-80 m at 8 s. Add top_keys [[3,90],[8,130],[30,450],[60,800],[180,1500]] to drive the late climb; note that head_state's max(keys-h, center*0.5) then needs the lower rise_k. In _conventional_fireball, keep center_y = base_y for CONVENTIONAL_SURFACE (no lerp toward the head until life > 0.9). In the head_state conventional branch, start appear at ~0.6*dur and clamp center_y >= half so the cloud base stays on the ground. Set stem_density ~0.25, stem_delay ~8 and stem_speed_rel >= 1.2 so any late pedestal stays attached.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The sky goes black for an 11 t HE blast at 8 km at noon. The log shows adapt 2.0 stops and maxc 4.0 at 0.4-1 s. The sky is (38,42,44) at 1 s, near black until 2 s, and teal-grey until 8 s. The same stop-down makes the flame a matte, pastel orange (174,84,0). When I brightened the 0.4 s frame 3x offline, it showed the correct yellow-white core with an orange rim, matching the 0.4 s reference.
issues.fix: In Explosion.metered_luminance, skip the cov/l_fb branch when prof.conventional (use lum = ill/amb only), set env_ctl.max_comp <= 1.0 for conventional bursts, and use a recovery tau of ~1 s. Then raise MOAB emission 260 -> ~350-400 so the core clips warm white-yellow while the rim stays orange.

issues.problem: [PARTLY FIXED] The flame now lasts about 2.4 s (fixed), but its shape and look are still wrong. Aspect is about 2.2:1 (520x225 px, ~80 m tall at 1 s) against 3.5-4:1 (140x40 m) in the reference. The surface looks like popcorn or cotton, with detached flecks around the silhouette. There is no luminous gradient: because kf=14/fb.w makes the flame opaque, only the lq~1 shell (tloc*0.86) is visible, so there is no white-hot core. At 0.005-0.06 s it is a cream-peach cotton ball, with no one-frame blue-white flash and no yellow-white dome spreading sideways.
issues.fix: Set fireball_squash 0.5 -> ~0.3. In _conventional_fireball, change base_y lift from r*0.55*(..) to r*squash*0.9 so the dome sits on the ground. Set fireball_noise 0.4 -> 0.3 and fireball_noise_scale 3.5 -> ~6 (finer turbulence, no flecks). In fireball_density, soften the edge from smoothstep(0.05,-0.12,dd) to smoothstep(0.15,-0.25,dd). For conventional, lower kf to ~5/fb.w (pass it via a uniform) so the hotter interior shows through. Add a <=0.03 s flash: temp ~6000 K and emission x3 for t < 0.03 s.

issues.problem: [NEW] A glowing horizontal belt (a 'lamp in a bell jar') runs across the lower half of the black smoke ball at 0.4-1 s. It comes from head heat_glow (emission*0.4*fb opacity) being emitted around the torus core ring rc (y = -0.25H), a feature that makes no physical sense for an HE smoke cloud.
issues.fix: In head_state's conventional branch, set heat_glow to 0 (or <= 0.1*emission) and let the flame volume carry the light. The existing fireball-light term (blackbody*fl*0.25*R^2/(d^2+R^2)) already warms the smoke's underside.

issues.problem: [REMAINS/WORSE] By 60 s it is a textbook nuclear mushroom: a dark cap on a thick, leaning, km-tall pipe stem, with horizontal spun-sugar striations on the cap. At 30 s the cap floats above a flat-topped stem. The dossier specifies a stemless cauliflower thermal about as tall as it is wide, then a ~0.5 km cap with 'no true stem'. The 60 s frame is also nearly identical to FOAB at 60 s, so the signature collides.
issues.fix: Set stem_density ~0.25, stem_radius_m 120 -> ~140 and stem_flare ~2.5 for a ragged, dusty pedestal rather than a pipe. Set torus 0.8 -> 0.3 (a buoyant thermal, not a vortex-ring mushroom). Raise head_noise_amp 0.55 -> 0.7 and billow_sharp 0.75 -> 1.4 for big cauliflower lobes. Set cap_half_m 260 -> ~200 so H is about R. For the striations, use rigid head drift (see systemic).

issues.problem: [PARTLY FIXED] The skirt colour now matches the ground, but the ground layers are still geometric. At 0.005-0.15 s a hard-edged grey 'puck' sits under the flame: this is the DustWallLayer cylinder inside the fireball. At 0.4 s there is a flat plank or tray with square ends. At 1-4 s a uniform tan band crosses the whole frame. The required 'visible wave ring' racing outward never reads. There is no condensation (wilson=0), although section 6.3 lists condensation and Eglin is humid.
issues.fix: In DustWallLayer.update: multiply op by smoothstep(1.3,1.8,r/fireball_radius), cap h at ~25 m for MOAB, require p > ~1 psi (op from (p-1)/4), and fade with exp(-(t-0.1)/1.2), so it reads as a thin, ragged ring sweeping to ~300-400 m during 0.1-1.5 s. Add a silhouette fade to dust_wall.gdshader. For condensation, set wilson ~0.4 with humid_site=True or wilson_force, wilson_duration ~0.25 s, rendered as a thin bright limb only.

issues.problem: Black debris cubes rain as uniform pepper specks in the gap under the ball at 2-4 s. The 8-60 s skirt is a long, straight-topped mound. The terrain shows two long white horizontal stripes in every frame.
issues.fix: Give debris a wide size distribution with dust trails and fewer visible specks (debris_count 600 -> ~250). Add azimuthal height noise to the skirt. Fix the terrain grazing-angle stripes (see systemic).

issues.problem: [REMAINS, cause changed] The cap is a rust-orange felt ball from 0.5 s to about 90 s, tan-pink after that. Cycle 1's 20 s glow is gone (core_cool_s 1.0 works), but the albedo is now rust: head_color_early [0.34,0.19,0.10], whitening only at about 100 s, warmed further by the low dawn sun. The film (lf1_ivyflats t1s/t22s) and the dossier show a white/grey boiling bell cloud from 0.6 s, then a white cap with tan dust underneath. It also makes DC look like B61, since both are rust balls at 2-40 s.
issues.fix: Set head_color_early [0.66,0.62,0.57], head_color_late [0.78,0.76,0.73], whiten_time 0.5 -> 0.05 and dark_base ~0.6 (tan underside). Keep stem_color [0.42,0.36,0.28] so the stem is dirtier than the cap.

issues.problem: [NEW] The historical time of day is wrong. tod_hist='dawn', but the dossier gives 17 July 1962, 10:00 PDT (sun ~55 deg). The dawn preset makes the sky olive-green overhead ((135,135,94) at 180 s) and lights everything orange from a low sun, which contradicts the bright daylight in the film reference.
issues.fix: Set davy_crockett tod_hist 'dawn' -> 'noon' (or add a 'morning' preset with ~50 deg sun). Also fix the dawn sky gradient in sky.gdshader, which mixes blue and orange into olive (it affects Trinity, Grable and the others).

issues.problem: [NEW/REMAINS systemic] The stem detaches. A flat-topped pipe stops ~1 cap radius below the cap at 10, 20 and 40 s, and they only rejoin at 90 s. In the film at 22 s and fig 8-1 at 20 s the stem runs continuously into the cap. The cause is stem_state's top = min(head_bottom+0.45*half, (t-t_start)*avg_speed*0.75): the stem rises at ~15 m/s while the head climbs faster.
issues.fix: For davy_crockett set stem_speed_rel ~1.6. Better, in stem_state, for non-detached bombs set top = head_bottom + 0.45*half once t > t_start + ~2 s. In stem_density, fade the top over ~3 radii (not 1.5) with noise-modulated height.

issues.problem: [NEW] The stem is a smooth 'candy-cane' or drinking straw: uniform width, bent in a perfectly smooth parabola by the shear pow(y/wind_h,1.7). The cap is a smooth bun. At 360 s the cap's left (upwind) side is cut by a hard vertical wall: the proxy box in Explosion._update_volume only extends by wind_v*t*1.5, while the shader shift reaches 1.5^1.7 = 1.99x. Horizontal streak bands cross the cap at 360 s.
issues.fix: In _update_volume, use drift = wind_v*t*2.05 plus the head radius as margin. In explosion_volume.gdshader, shift the head rigidly (evaluate the drift at head.y for head lookups) and shear only the stem. Add a per-height noise term to the stem shear (about +/-15% of the drift, wavelength ~3 stem radii) so it waves like the film's 'wavy dusty stem'.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The skirt is a flat slab or tray, with a vertical blue-grey shaded front face, square ends, a flat top about 1/4 of the ball's height, and a knife-straight shadow boundary across it (1-10 s). The film shows a thin, bright horizontal dust line along the ground. Growth is now bounded (fixed).
issues.fix: Set skirt_height ~0.35. In sdf_skirt, taper prof to 0 at x -> 1 with a rounded front, and stop the -p.y-h*0.15 floor from showing as a wall. Add azimuthal height noise. In cheap_density, soften the skirt term from /(skirt.y*0.4) to /(skirt.y*1.2) to remove the knife-edge shadow.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] Incandescence ends after 0.1 s. At 0.5 s the ball is a matte rust dome with no glow, while the dossier says it glows from yellow to orange-red until ~0.6 s. The cause: the head appears at 10-40 t2 (0.07-0.29 s) with r_now = 1.04*r_fb, wrapping the fireball in an opaque, non-emissive shell.
issues.fix: For sub-kt surface bursts, delay the head's appear to ~0.5-0.6 s, or keep the head radius at 0.85*r_fb while fs.opacity > 0.3. Set core_glow 0.3 -> 0.6 with core_cool_s 1.0 so the core shows orange-red through ~0.6 s, then the cloud turns white.

issues.problem: [PARTLY FIXED] There is no full-frame white-out. The log shows flash=0.2-0.3 (B61 reaches 2.1), and the 0.002/0.02 s frames are an ordinary pale sky with a glowing hemisphere. The dossier film shows a full camera white-out for ~0.1-0.17 s.
issues.fix: Drive env white_out for t < ~0.15 s for nuclear bursts based on the fireball's angular size and transmittance, not yield^0.3 alone, so the 18 t burst at 8 km in the binocular view whites out.

issues.problem: Uniform dark debris specks hang around the ball at 1-5 s like a swarm of flies. At 90-360 s there is a hard horizontal terrain seam near the bottom of the frame, with an orange speckled band below it. The cycle-1 black bunker bar at 180/360 s is fixed.
issues.fix: Reduce debris_count 1200 -> ~400, use a wider size spread and fall them out faster. Fix the terrain near-LOD/texture seam (see systemic).

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The section 6.3 signature, a 'huge rolling orange ball lasting 8-9 s', is lost after ~2 s. The 2 s frame is good: fire inside soot rolls, one body (the cycle-1 snowman is fixed). By 3 s, though, the flame is mostly buried under an opaque black shell, at 5 s only a few embers show, and at 7 s there is just a small red lick at the base. The dossier: orange to red with black soot rolls over 1.5-5 s, flames out at 5-8 s. The cause: the conventional head appears at 0.15*dur = 1.3 s with r_now = 1.05*r_fb, enclosing the flame (which is still at ~0.9 r), and the skin starts at life 0.2.
issues.fix: In head_state for THERMOBARIC, start appear at ~0.45*dur and use r_now = 0.8*r_fb while fs.opacity > 0.3, so flames lick out through the soot. Set skin = clamp((life-0.45)/0.45). In head_density, multiply dens by (1 - 0.7*smoothstep(1.1,0.7,|p-fb|/fb.w)*fb opacity) so soot appears as rolls and patches inside the flame (as in the BLU-82 reference) rather than as a lid.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The documented FAE phases are still missing. There is no grey aerosol pancake (about 100 m wide, 10-15 m thick) for 0-0.15 s, and no whole-cloud yellow-white flash at 0.15-0.25 s. At 0.05 s there is already a round, ~40 m popcorn fireball, so it reads as an HE blast, not a fuel-air one.
issues.fix: Add an aerosol phase in _conventional_fireball for THERMOBARIC: for t < 0.15 s return opacity 0 and draw the skirt sdf as a disc (r 50 m, h 12 m, grey [0.55,0.55,0.52], no emission), or add a new 'aerosol' uniform. For 0.15-0.25 s, set the fb radius to 50 m at once with squash ~0.25, temp ~3300 K and emission x3, then grow it into the dome.

issues.problem: [NEW] The ball is too small and too round early: about 70-85 m across at 1 s with aspect ~1.45:1. The dossier wants a flattened, ground-hugging dome about 120 m x 70 m by 0.25-1.5 s. Growth is too slow because t_grow = t_fb_max = 0.3*8.65 = 2.6 s for THERMOBARIC.
issues.fix: Add a fb_grow_s override (~0.8 s) for t_grow in _conventional_fireball. Set foab fireball_squash ~0.6 and base_y = hob + r*squash*0.9 so the dome base touches the ground. Raise fireball_noise_scale 2.4 -> ~4 for rolling lobes.

issues.problem: [WORSE] The smoke is a flat black cut-out: core (17,18,21), best lit side (39-53). No sunlit side, lobes or billows read; it looks like a hole in the sky. The palette's #2A2522 is the lit smoke colour, and real black smoke in noon sun shows brown-grey highlights and distinct lobe shading.
issues.fix: Set head_color_late [0.12,0.11,0.10] -> ~[0.20,0.18,0.16] and whiten_time 5 -> ~1.5, so the smoke greys slowly after a minute. Raise billow_sharp to ~1.4 for distinct lobes. Add an albedo-scaled multiple-scattering term in explosion_volume (light += sun_c*0.15*albedo*(1-far_s)) so dark media keep some relief.

issues.problem: [REMAINS/WORSE] The 'little dust' signature is violated. At 2-15 s a massive, opaque grey-white dust band (the DustWall open cylinder) crosses the entire frame width, 60-90 px tall. At 30-60 s an ~0.8 km flat mound remains. A faint glass slab with square ends sits on the horizon at 0.5 s.
issues.fix: Set dust_wall 0.6 -> 0.15, skirt 0.4 -> 0.15 and skirt_max_r 350 -> ~200, and apply the systemic DustWallLayer fixes (threshold, height cap, fade after passage, silhouette fade).

issues.problem: [PARTLY FIXED] The cycle-1 pencil-thin lollipop is gone, but the result is a textbook nuclear mushroom: a thick stem from the ground to a round black cap, nearly identical to MOAB at 60 s. A hard horizontal tone step crosses the stem just below the cap: grey 24 above, tan 57 below, within ~20 px at y~425 in the 60 s frame. This is the knife-edge cheap_density shadow of the cap. Horizontal streaks run across the cap top at 15 s and 60 s. The dossier: a short-stemmed mushroom by ~5 s that leaves a dark smoke ball rising to ~2 km.
issues.fix: Set stem_density 0.4 -> ~0.15 and add a stem fade (a col_fade-like key in stem_state for non-column kinds) to 0 between ~20 and 40 s. In cheap_density, soften the head term from /(head_shape.x*0.25) to /(head_shape.x*0.8) so the cap's shadow on the stem is a gradient. For the streaks, use rigid head drift (see systemic).

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The noon sky goes charcoal ((60,64,70) at 1 s, darker at 2-7 s). The log shows adapt up to 1.97 stops and maxc 4.0. The dossier says 'Little exposure blow-out'.
issues.fix: Use the conventional exposure fix (no cov stop-down for prof.conventional, max_comp <= 1).

issues.problem: [NEW] At 7 s the flame remnant at the base is a neon, fully saturated red that looks like CG. The temperature lerps down to 1300 K, and the film saturation boost bc = mix(bc, pow(bc,1.7), 0.55) pushes it to pure red.
issues.fix: Floor the end temperature at ~1500 K, fade the opacity over life 0.8-1.1, and in the shader reduce the pow(bc,1.7) mix for tloc < 1800 K.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] A faint pen-line hemisphere outline of the shock shell (rim alpha) surrounds the ball at 0.05-0.5 s.
issues.fix: See the systemic shock-rim fix: scale strength by the front's angular thickness, and use ~0.2x for conventional and sub-kt bursts.

issues.problem: [REMAINS, changed] The cloud is a perfectly round 'pom-pom' or felt ball, covered in fine isotropic fuzz, and its silhouette barely changes from 2 s to 90 s. Able (the colour reference) is a lumpy, irregular, multi-lobed cloud. Wasp is a flattened cap with tendrils hanging underneath. Neither the lumpy character nor the cap flattening appears.
issues.fix: Set head_noise_amp 0.5 -> 0.7, billow_sharp 1.0 -> 1.6 and head_noise_scale (head_heat.w) 0.55 -> ~0.35 for bigger, distinct lobes. In head_density, reduce the b3 octave weight 0.10 -> 0.04 (less fur) and raise the od_local self-shadow so crevices go dark. Flatten the cap toward H ~ 0.5R by 60 s (cap_aspect_max 0.75 -> 0.5). Add underside tendrils with negative-y noise on the dark_base region.

issues.problem: [WORSE] Late in the shot the cap becomes swirled brush-stroke strands, with a thin, detached elliptical halo line around its top and a 'combed' black underside. This happens because the shader shears the noise domain with p.xz -= wind*age*pow(clamp(y/wind_h,0,1.5),1.7), and the clamp kink at 1.5*wind_h (~1.6 km) falls inside the cap; the roll rotation (2.2 rad) adds to it.
issues.fix: Shift the head rigidly: evaluate the drift at head.y for every head lookup and shear only the stem, with no clamp kink inside the cap. Lower roll 2.2 -> ~0.8 for this small-torus bomb (torus 0.5).

issues.problem: [REMAINS, changed] The column is now detached (fixed), but it is a smooth, uniform grey-beige 'tin can' or chimney with a flat top at 2-40 s, and a smooth bent rod later. It is lighter (140,126,108) than the turbulent, dark, lumpy Wasp column with its puffy cauliflower head and boiling dust base.
issues.fix: Set stem_stretch (stem_col.w) to 1.0. In stem_density, raise the lf weight 0.7 -> 1.2 and the amplitude 0.6r -> 0.9r. Fade the top over 3-4 radii with noise and add a puff (an ellipsoid of ~1.6 r) at the column top. Set stem_color to ~[0.38,0.32,0.25] and stem_flare ~2.0 so a wide dust foot boils at the base.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] The sky and ground go pitch black ((8-12) sRGB) at 0.1-1 s and stay slate until about 5 s. The log shows adapt 3.3 stops for a 0.3 kt burst at 12 km. The spec allows 3-8 stops, but a black sky over black ground makes these frames unreadable. At 0.1 s the ball is still a clipped white disc with an orange halo, with no rapatronic mottling.
issues.fix: Make the cov stop-down act only for t < 3*t2 (~0.075 s). For W < 1 kt, cap max_comp at ~2.5 and use a recovery tau of ~1 s. Lower glow on the fireball in zoom and raise the fb_shape.y mottle amplitude so the surface reads.

issues.problem: [REMAINS] A full-width grey band (the DustWall cylinder) crosses the frame at 1-10 s, and a flat mound sits on the horizon at 20-40 s. A 150 m airburst of 0.3 kt should leave only a low, faint tan precursor skirt around the column foot.
issues.fix: Set dust_wall 0.5 -> ~0.2, skirt 0.25 -> 0.15 and a tan dust_color [0.50,0.43,0.34], and apply the systemic DustWallLayer fixes.

issues.problem: [NEW] Shadows crush to near black under a noon desert sky. The ball's shadow side is (23,22,24) at 10 s, against (176,126,89) on the lit side, and at 180-360 s the cap is a white top over a black storm-cloud underside. This is an over-correction of cycle 1's 'too flat' lighting: ambient and ground bounce are now too weak.
issues.fix: In explosion_volume.gdshader raise amb*ao*0.6 -> ~0.9 with an ao floor of 0.35, ground bounce 0.18 -> ~0.35, and add albedo-scaled multiple scattering, so the shaded sides of light clouds sit at ~25-35% of the lit side.

issues.problem: [NEW] The section 6.3 signature lists 'a Wilson dome', but none is visible. Only faint shock-rim arcs appear at the frame edges, and only when the 0.5 s frame is brightened. WilsonLayer gates amount by (humidity-0.45)/0.35, which is zero on the desert preset.
issues.fix: Give b61_12 a forced minimum (for example wilson_force with amount ~0.35, wilson_duration ~0.5) rendered as a thin, bright, sunlit limb veil. Alternatively, remove the dome from the signature text so the game does not promise it.

issues.problem: [PARTLY FIXED] The NO2 red-brown is now present (fixed), but it is a light, saturated orange 'suede' (176,126,89) rather than Able's dark chocolate red-brown. At 0.5 s the dull-red ball has a pixel-scale glitter or sequin texture from high-frequency skin/patch noise.
issues.fix: Set head_color_early [0.48,0.23,0.13] -> ~[0.32,0.15,0.09]. In fireball_density, lower the patch noise frequency for the skin (nbl(nq*0.9) -> nq*0.5, drop the nq*2.6 octave weight).

issues.problem: The exposure crush REMAINS. It has improved since cycle 1: the sky is back, dim brown, by 5 s and normal by 10 s, where cycle 1 stayed dark to 20 s. The log shows adapt = 7.85 / 7.24 / 5.75 stops at 0.5 / 1 / 2 s with maxc 8.7, so sky and ground are pure black (0,0,0). The 2 s frame is a dim red ember (62,4,0) in a black frame and reads as a night test. Cause: the zoom auto-frame fills the view with the ball, so in Explosion.metered_luminance cov goes to about 1, max_comp = lerp(6,10,cov) and the meter locks onto the fireball's surface luminance l_fb.
issues.fix: In metered_luminance: for nuclear bursts use max_comp = lerp(4.5, 6.0, cov) and clamp cov to 0.35, since the auto-zoom is not the eye being filled. Multiply l_fb by smoothstep(3000, 6000, temp). Once t > 3*t2, limit adapt_log so that the sky stays at 40/255 or more. Target: at 1 s the sky and range are visible and the ball is the brightest thing in frame.

issues.problem: Grable is rendered in the wrong time of day and on a broken dawn sky. The dossier gives 08:29 with the sun 34 deg up in the E and a clear blue sky with cirrus, but tod_hist='dawn' uses the DAWN preset (sun el 1.6 deg, orange sun_col). The result is an olive-green/khaki sky (zenith (169,154,112) at 20 s, (94,103,81) at 360 s), orange 'Mars dune' foreground sand, raking orange side light and a salmon-pink cloud. Nothing matches the blue-sky colour references.
issues.fix: Add a 'morning' preset (el 32-35 deg, az about 100 deg, near-white sun) and set grable tod_hist='morning' (or 'noon'). Separately, fix the DAWN sky in sky.gdshader scatter(): add ozone absorption (BETA_O = vec3(0.65e-6, 1.88e-6, 0.085e-6) with a tent density peaking at 25 km, added to tau). Change DAWN fog_col from (0.42,0.38,0.40) to about (0.30,0.34,0.46) so the twilight zenith stays blue, not green.

issues.problem: Phallic 'tower plus knob' silhouette, which is a real YouTube risk. The stem is as wide as the cap: about 0.9x cap width at 90 s, 0.8x at 180 s (170 px vs 215 px) and 0.53x at 360 s. It has a 2.4x trumpet base, and the cap is a small knob with a rolled rim. In the colour references the stem is about 0.25-0.3 of the cap. Cause: BlastPhysics.stem_radius() = 0.5 x the FINAL cap_r at 15 kt. stem_state reaches it at 0.4*t_stab (about 130 s), while head_state reaches the full cap width only at t_stab (about 325 s).
issues.fix: In ExplosionProfile.stem_state use radius = min(stem_r, 0.32*head_state(t).radius). In BlastPhysics.stem_radius change the factor to clamp(0.3 - 0.1*log10(W/20), 0.1, 0.3). For grable set stem_radius_m about 450 and stem_flare 2.4 -> 1.7.

issues.problem: The low-burst signature (section 6.3: 'Mach stem, precursor, ragged dusty front') is still not visible in any frame (REMAINS). At 0.1 s there is only a clipped white disc whose flat bottom is the ground clip. There is no pale reflected-shock dome under it at 0.07-0.10 s and no bright Mach-stem band. In the precursor phase (0.15-3 s) there is no ragged, jetting dark-tan dust wall racing out to 1.6 km and no popcorning or fuming ground; at 0.5-2 s everything below the ball is black.
issues.fix: After the exposure fix, make the precursor read. In DustWallLayer.update use op = clampf((p-0.3)/1.0, 0, 1) when precursor=true, set dust_color [0.42,0.35,0.27], and in dust_wall.gdshader give ragged=1 jets with height-noise amplitude 0.8 h. In shockwave.gdshader draw the stem band as an opaque bright grey-white band (alpha 1.0, not refraction) while t < 0.4 s. Add the reflected-shock dome as a thin translucent pale shell (sdf_shell centred on the ground, r about 1.1*hob, opacity 0.3, 0.06-0.25 s), and set grable reflect_cut_t = 0.07 so fireball_cut_y flattens the ball's bottom by 0.10 s.

issues.problem: The fireball looks like a crumpet, sponge or cork board: uniform fixed-size cellular blotches across the whole disc, no limb darkening, no hotter core and a ragged flame fringe. Its colour runs peach (0.5 s) -> orange (1 s) -> dark-red ember (2 s). The dossier gives yellow, then orange over 1-5 s. Cycle 1 had a white disc and peach until 10 s, so the cooling has been over-corrected. Cause, in the shader emission: fpatch comes from Worley nbl() at a fixed nq scale and drives tloc x0.70..1.18 (about 8x luminance contrast between cells), and bc = mix(bc, pow(bc,1.7), 0.55) over-saturates.
issues.fix: In explosion_volume.gdshader use tloc factor mix(0.88, 1.06, ...). Take fpatch from nlf(nq*0.45) with a domain warp (3-5 large convective cells). Add limb darkening lum *= mix(1.0, 0.6, smoothstep(0.75, 1.0, lq)) and reduce the saturation push 0.55 -> 0.25. Keep fb_look.z (edge noise) at 0.08 or less until 1 s. In fireball_state, fade_time smoothstep(4,12 t_fb_max) -> (6,20) so the visible ball stays at 3500 K or more until about 3 s.

issues.problem: At 5 s the ball is a matte brick-red felt pom-pom. The head_heat glow shows only as a dim 'jack-o-lantern grin' band in its lower third, not the brilliant orange equatorial toroid in both colour references. At 10-40 s it becomes a salmon cotton egg with no NOx orange-brown lumps and weak sun/shade. It floats detached above the stem with a gap of 60-130 px of empty sky (10-40 s).
issues.fix: In head_density, stop reducing density with the 'hot' term (dens *= 1-0.75*hot). Instead add emission on the outer surface of the rolling vortex: glow is proportional to exp(-pow(rc.y/(0.3*H),2)) * smoothstep(0.45, 1.0, rxz/R). grable profile: core_glow 0.5 -> 1.2, core_cool_s 13 -> 25, head_color_early [0.36,0.20,0.09], head_noise_amp 0.5, billow_sharp 1.3. Close the gap: stem_speed_rel 0.75 -> 1.2, and for precursor/dusty bursts attach the stem top to head_bottom + half*0.45 from about 6 s.

issues.problem: The stem is a blurred rectangular box: flat top, vertical walls and soft vertical streaks; at 40 s it has a flat-cut chimney top. Its colour has improved since cycle 1 (no longer blue gauze), but with albedo 0.13 it still renders mid grey-brown (RGB 100-150) instead of the near-black brown column in the references, and it has no lumps.
issues.fix: Fade the stem top over about 3 radii with noise in stem_density (smoothstep(stem.y + 0.5r, stem.y - 3r*(0.6 + 0.8*lf), p.y)). Add big bulges: dn -= (nlf(np*0.15)-0.5)*r*0.8. For dense dark media, cut the stem ambient (amb*ao*0.6 -> 0.3 when ds dominates) and lower the fog blend fog.a*0.65 -> 0.4.

issues.problem: The skirt is a flat-topped slab with a hard horizontal bottom edge and a hard vertical light/shadow split: grey-blue left, cream right, (153,141,139) vs (203,183,169) at 20 s. At 5 s, layered stripes appear: a dust band, a dark 'lake' band and a light band. From 90 s it is a flat white rim under the stem. No billowing, no black smoke patches, no lingering dust storm.
issues.fix: In skirt_density, modulate height by (0.6 + 0.8*nlf(p.xz/(R*0.15))) and add 6-10 rising billow plumes with darker SOOT patches where kn < 0.35. Soften the stem shadow on the skirt: in cheap_density use stem.z*1.2 instead of stem.z*0.4. Fade the DustWall once the skirt exists (op *= 1 - smoothstep(t_hit+3, t_hit+10, t)).

issues.problem: The screen-space rectangular seam from cycle 1 REMAINS. At 5 s there is a hard vertical brightness step exactly at x=800 (frame centre) from y about 620 to 745, and horizontal steps at y about 647 and 670 inside the dust/terrain band: (90,73,68) left vs (110,86,76) right.
issues.fix: Re-render with --noglass and -vdebug to isolate it. The likely cause is the depth_tex soft fade (dust_wall.gdshader and explosion_volume both reconstruct scene_t) reading bunker glass/frame depth or a tiled buffer. Exclude the bunker layer from the depth used for the fade, or render it in a separate pass.

issues.problem: There are no ice caps or 'ice skirt' (3 successive pileus, reference UK-53-128); the profile has no ice_cap or tier2 keys (REMAINS). Wind shear now exists (the column leans at 180-360 s), which is PARTLY FIXED but much weaker than the violent NE shear in the dossier. The late cap is a smooth knob covered in concentric horizontal 'spun-sugar' streaks, with no cauliflower.
issues.fix: Add ice_cap {t_on:0.25, dur:0.6, opacity:0.5, r_rel:1.05} and tier2 {t_on:0.45, dur:0.8, opacity:0.4, radius_m:1600, height_rel:0.55, half_m:250}. Raise wind to about [6,-6] with wind_h about 6000. Drop 'roll' 2.2 -> 0.6 (the radius-dependent roll rotation shears the noise into streaks; see systemic).

issues.problem: White 'firefly' speckles along the limb REMAIN. With the bloom and the rough edge, the ball reads about 20% too big: R about 128 m at 20 ms vs 107 m (510*t^0.4), and about 200 m at 0.1 s vs 170 m at the 0.13 s maximum.
issues.fix: Gate emission by smoothstep(0.3, 0.8, df), add a per-sample HDR clamp, and keep fb_look.z at 0.1 or less before t2.

issues.problem: The iconic props are missing: the white zig-zag smoke-rocket trails and the black/white smoke screens that kink as the precursor passes. These make Grable instantly recognizable in both colour references.
issues.fix: Optional: add 8-12 thin white trail meshes about 1-3 km right of GZ whose vertices are displaced sideways when shock_ground_radius passes them.

issues.problem: The exposure crush REMAINS (improved: dark teal at 5 s, near normal at 10 s). The log shows adapt 6.38 / 5.78 / 4.33 stops at 0.5 / 1 / 2 s with maxc 7.0, so the noon sky and ground are pure black. The 2 s frame is a dim red disc in a black frame with the ground barely visible. At 0.1 s the frame is a uniform grey (sky and ground both about 97,95,93) and the horizon has vanished.
issues.fix: Apply the systemic metering fix: max_comp = lerp(4.5, 6.0, cov), cov clamped to 0.35, l_fb weighted by smoothstep(3000, 6000, T). Also reduce the flash fog/bloom at the second maximum so the horizon line survives.

issues.problem: The fireball is too dim and too cool. The dossier says 'brilliant white sphere growing to ~380 m across at 1 s'. The render is a peach crumpet at 0.5 s, a saturated orange crumpet at 1 s ((138,63,1)) and a dark red ember at 2 s. The size at 1 s is correct (about 380 m). The same crumpet/cork cellular texture appears as on Grable, with no limb darkening and no core.
issues.fix: Use the same fireball-shader fix as Grable: lower patch contrast, use large convective cells, add limb darkening and reduce the saturation push. Make sure the ball renders yellow-white (T about 5000 K) at 1 s and yellow-orange at 2-3 s. Do not let the exposure stop down onto the ball (see systemic).

issues.problem: The condensation signature is gone. Section 6.3 asks for 'a shock wave with condensation'. Cycle 1 had a CG glass ball; that artifact is gone, but so is the feature, so this is a signature REGRESSION. Cause: shot_rig sets Game.humidity = 0.35, so WilsonLayer.amount = clamp((0.35-0.45)/0.35) * wilson = 0, even though the profile has wilson=1.0. Hiroshima in August was humid.
issues.fix: Add a per-bomb site_humidity key (little_boy 0.8) and apply it in main.prepare_world / env_ctl.set_humidity unless --humidity is passed. In wilson.gdshader, keep the veil to the upper bell (a *= smoothstep(-0.1, 0.4, v_local.y)), punch soft holes (a *= smoothstep(0.35, 0.6, nz)), add a 0.2 fill term on top of the limb, cap alpha at 0.4, and set wilson_duration about 0.7.

issues.problem: The cap is a maroon/raspberry-purple cotton pom-pom ((74,56,61) at 20 s) with a near-black underside, unchanged for 1.5 minutes. The dossier says 'white outside, purplish-black inside with a fiery red core'; the purple has been put on the OUTSIDE. Cause: head_color_early [0.20,0.11,0.13] with whiten_time 1.0. col_mix = (x-0.04)/1.0 with t_stab about 325 s, so the cap is only about 24% whitened at 90 s. This is WORSE than the cycle-1 pink egg.
issues.fix: head_color_early [0.62,0.55,0.55] -> head_color_late [0.88,0.87,0.86], whiten_time 0.12. Show the 'purplish-black inside' through crevices and the underside only (dark_base 0.7 plus a purple tint on lowk shading). Show the red core through gaps: core_radius 0.25, core_glow 0.8, core_cool_s about 20.

issues.problem: The cap floats detached above a translucent, flat-topped grey 'box' stem from 10 s to 90 s. The box has a hard vertical light/shadow split down the middle ((59,63,68) left vs (153,149,147) right at 20 s) and a visible gap below the cap through 90 s. For a 600 m airburst the stem should be a narrow inflow column that thickens and joins the cap (1.6 km cloud at 18 s).
issues.fix: For non-dusty airbursts, start the stem radius at 0.08*stem_r and grow it with sqrt(rx); stem_speed_rel 0.75 -> 1.2, joining the head bottom by about 30 s. Soften the stem terminator: macro_s = 0.35 + 0.65*smoothstep(-0.6, 0.8, dot(vec3(nr.x, 0.15, nr.y), L)). Fade the top over about 3 radii.

issues.problem: The late cloud is a smooth 'hamburger bun' with concentric spun-sugar striations across the top, a near-black underside ((16,20,25) at 360 s) and a uniform smooth tube stem. The Caron photo shows a white cauliflower with deep, sharply defined lobes and a lumpy stem with secondary bulges. The stem is about 0.84 of the cap width at 90 s, giving an 'i' silhouette; the cap is detached at 90 s.
issues.fix: roll 2.2 -> 0.5 (see systemic), head_noise_amp 0.3 -> 0.5, billow_sharp 1.3. Raise the multiple-scattering floor and the ground-bounce term so undersides read mid grey (see systemic). Add stem bulges (large nlf displacement) and apply the stem-radius tie to the head radius (0.32*R).

issues.problem: The city dust and smoke layer is a uniform dark-brown 'hedgerow' band of constant height, with a fine fuzzy top, spanning the full frame width (5-20 s). Later it becomes a flat brown pancake (40-180 s). Its colour has improved since cycle 1 (no longer a white puck), but it has no boiling, no black smoke plumes, no fires and no NW drift.
issues.fix: In skirt_density, add large-scale height modulation (nlf at 400-600 m cells, amplitude about 1.5*h). Add 10-20 local smoke plumes 200-800 m tall from about 5 s, with SOOT albedo. Add emissive orange fire points at p.y < 20 m where nlf > 0.7 from about 5 s, plus slow growth to 3 km and NW drift via wind.

issues.problem: The brief dim orange shell at the thermal minimum (8.5 ms) and the double pulse are not visible: 2 ms and 20 ms are both white balls in a pale grey sky.
issues.fix: Shoot a frame at 0.008 s, let the exposure stay put through the dip, and render the ball dim orange there (fireball_temperature already gives about 3300 K).

issues.problem: Two thin bright 'painted' stripes or ellipses lie across the foreground terrain. This is the terrain shock-ring decal or texture banding, not a dust ring sweeping out.
issues.fix: Render the ground shock as a soft raised dust band (DustWall or volume), not as a bright line in terrain.gdshader. Anisotropic filtering and detail noise are needed for the foreground streaks.

issues.problem: No 'smoking ground' or heat haze for about 3 s after the pulse, and no optional firestorm or black-rain phase (REMAINS).
issues.fix: Drive a short-lived ground smoke/haze sheet from g_scorch, and optionally a late pyrocumulus.

issues.problem: The scene is not pre-dawn. The dossier gives 05:29 with the sun below the horizon, a deep blue-violet sky, a pale ENE band and a broken cloud deck overhead lit red-orange by the fireball (Aeby photo) with a hole punched through it; only the cloud top catches the sun, at about 20 min. The DAWN preset puts the sun at +1.6 deg with base exposure 1.5. From 10 s on this gives a khaki/olive daylight sky (zenith (102,110,83)), a cloud side-lit by the sun, an orange dune foreground and no cloud deck. It looks like an afternoon in a dust storm.
issues.fix: Add a 'predawn' preset: sun el -4 deg with no direct sun on the ground. In explosion_volume, gate sun_c by the earth-shadow height (smoothstep(h_sh - 500, h_sh + 500, p.y), h_sh about 6-8 km) so only the high cloud catches sunlight. Use a twilight sky (deep blue zenith, pale ENE glow), with the ozone fix in sky.gdshader. Let the fireball be the main light (g_fireball_color). Add a broken stratocumulus deck at 3-4 km lit by the fireball, with a hole opening at about 5-10 s.

issues.problem: The exposure crush is worst on this bomb: adapt 8.48 stops at 0.5 s, maxc 10.0, so the frames are pure black. The ball is a pink-lilac crumpet at 0.5 s, terracotta at 1 s ((101,44,28)) and dim orange at 2 s. The additive violet fb_tint ([0.55,0.35,0.95,0.5], tint_time 4 s) washes the whole ball pastel mauve. That is not the documented colour: blue-violet only in the first-ms flash, a violet radioluminescent haze around the cloud at about 25-35 s, and a white second peak yellowing to orange in between.
issues.fix: Apply the systemic metering fix. Restrict fb_tint to the flash (tint_time 4.0 -> 0.01). Add a separate 'violet_glow' halo emission around the head (colour [0.55,0.35,0.95], 25-35 s, about 0.3 of the sun term), not on the ball. Use the Grable crumpet/limb fix for texture.

issues.problem: The rapatronic stage is still missing (REMAINS). The geometry bug is FIXED: the hemisphere now sits on the ground. At 20 ms, though, the frame is a clipped white half-disc with a RAGGED popcorn top limb, firefly speckles and no mottling, which is the inverse of the 16 ms reference: a smooth limb, a mottled grey interior, and a bright lumpy 'popcorn' skirt plus Mach belt only at the base. There is no curtain line and no dark NOx front.
issues.fix: Before 0.1 s, set fb_look.z (edge noise) to about 0.02 for a smooth limb and meter the dome only about 1 stop over (adapt target on the dome) so the mottling (mottle_t2 6) shows. Implement skirt_early as a lumpy torus at r about 0.95R, h about 0.12R with nbl(np*4) lumps and emission 0.6x the fireball's, 2-100 ms. Draw the Mach belt brighter (shockwave stem band, alpha 1.0, until 100 ms).

issues.problem: The colour is wrong. At 5 s the head is a dull dark-red felt ball ((53,17,10)) with a faint 'jack-o-lantern' band, and at 10 s a matte salmon cotton ball. The Aeby colour still and the 10 s photo show a brilliant, self-luminous yellow-orange-white boiling cauliflower that lights the cloud deck. The dossier puts 'dull red' only at about 30 s.
issues.fix: trinity profile: core_glow 0.6 -> 1.5, core_radius about 0.6 (the whole ball boils and glows) for 1-12 s, core_cool_s about 30. Extend the fireball opacity fade (4-12 -> 8-25 t_fb_max). head_noise_amp 0.55 and billow_sharp 1.4 so the lobes read. head_color_early [0.42,0.17,0.07].

issues.problem: The cloud is a generic copy of Grable: the 90-360 s frames of Trinity and Grable are nearly indistinguishable (same tower-and-knob proportions, same lean, same olive sky and orange ground). The stem is about 0.8 of the cap width at 90 s and 0.6 at 180 s, a phallic silhouette. Missing: the neck and vortex ring at 3.5 s, the left-handed stem twist, the two fog rings, and the three-layer cloud (NE dust sheet, inversion layer at about 3.8 km, 4.5 km NW-drifting cap). The cap carries the same spun-sugar striations.
issues.fix: Add tier2 {t_on:0.08, dur:3.0, opacity:0.5, radius_m:3000, height_rel:0.36, half_m:350} tinted brown, and ring_list [[5,10,1500,450,60],[6,10,2100,500,60]]. Twist the stem: in stem_density rotate np.xz by p.y/stem.z*0.6. Use separate drift for the low layer (NE) and the cap (NW): add a second wind vector below wind_h. Apply the stem-radius fix (0.32*head R). roll -> 0.6.

issues.problem: The dust skirt and dust wall form stacked horizontal stripes at 5 s (tan band over a dark band over a light band), then a flat slab with a hard grey/cream split and vertical ends (10-40 s). There is no dust 'eating in from below' the dome, and from 90 s only a thin white rim remains.
issues.fix: Fade the DustWall once the skirt forms (op *= 1 - smoothstep(t_hit+3, t_hit+10, t)). Add height noise and plumes to skirt_density as for Grable. skirt_color [0.55,0.47,0.38], dust_color [0.50,0.43,0.35].

issues.problem: The stem is a wide, translucent, flat-topped curtain under the ball (10-20 s) and a detached flat-topped box with a gap under the cap at 40 s.
issues.fix: Same as Grable: join the stem to the head bottom (stem_speed_rel 1.2), fade the top over about 3 r with noise, and grow the radius with the head (0.32*R).

issues.problem: Firefly speckles along the dome limb REMAIN. Trinitite and the crater are not verifiable from the 25 km zoom view.
issues.fix: Emission gate plus HDR clamp (systemic). Add a near or low director shot to the review set for the crater and trinitite disc.

issues.problem: There is still no lagoon (REMAINS). The foreground is heavily streaked desert sand, and the 4.2 km pond seen from 25 km is a sliver that renders as broken black/blue dashed scanlines along the horizon in every frame (z-fight or aliasing at a grazing angle). At 240 s a hairline black line runs across the whole surge at y about 755. There are no ships for scale, no glitter path, no waves and no slick.
issues.fix: Set Baker rec_km 25 -> about 6 km (the reference photos were taken from Bikini island at 5.6 km; the surge stops at about 2.6 km) and pond_radius_m to at least rec_km + 3 km, or use a sea plane up to the bunker. Fix the pond/terrain z-fight by lifting the water about 0.3 m and clipping terrain under the pond. Add 10-20 ship silhouettes at 0.3-3 km, a sun glitter path, and the ring-wave train from the dossier's R(t) table.

issues.problem: The Wilson hemisphere, THE Baker signature, is completely absent; cycle 1 had a glass dome, now there is nothing. Cause: shot_rig sets humidity 0.35, so WilsonLayer.amount = clamp((0.35-0.45)/0.35) = 0. wilson_force only bypasses the >150 kt rule, and humid_site=True does not set humidity. Even when enabled, wilson.gdshader is limb-only (pow(1-facing,3)) and cannot produce reference 04's milky, nearly opaque 1.6 km dome with the crown poking through. The only remaining trace is the shock-rim hairline arc.
issues.fix: Make humid_site set site_humidity 0.85 (applied in main.prepare_world unless --humidity is given). In wilson.gdshader add a fill mode: a = mix(limb_a, 0.15 + 0.7*smoothstep(0.2, 0.7, nz), wilson_fill), with wilson_fill = 1 for Baker. Clear it bottom-up: discard where v_local.y*radius < ground_y + lerp(0, 0.8*radius, smoothstep(2.0, 3.5, t)). Add the remnant sheet as tier2 {radius 1.8 km, height about 700 m, half 80 m, fading by 15 s}. wilson_duration 1.6 -> 0.9.

issues.problem: The first second is still wrong (REMAINS). At 0.02 s the frame is empty: no blue-white underwater glow, no dark slick ring racing out, no white crack disk, no spray dome with a fireball glint (reference 02). By 0.2 s there is already a 650 m wide cotton cumulus egg. Cause: in _column_head, r = col_cap_r*(0.35 + 0.65*grow) from t=0 and there is no cap_appear. At 0.6 s it is a full cartoon mushroom with an 820 m cap, while the cauliflower should form only at 3-5 s. The column top is 506 m at 0.75 s against 640 m in the dossier (col_rise 7 unchanged).
issues.fix: baker: cap_appear 3.0. In _column_head use r = lerp(col_radius*1.05, cap, smoothstep(1.0, 5.0, t)). col_rise 7 -> 5.5. Add a smooth white spray-dome primitive (0.004-0.3 s) with an emissive glint on top for 0-50 ms. Add water decals: a dark slick ring at r = 1500*t (60 m wide) followed by a white crack disk.

issues.problem: The column and cap read as a 'cartoon mushroom': a cotton-wool pillar under a puffy, smooth ellipsoid cap, with a hard vertical sun/shade split on the column ((88,95,105) vs (209,209,208) at 8 s). Reference 01 shows a broad, straight-walled, hollow column with vertical streaks and spike jets, a flat top, a ragged crown, the dark 'Arkansas' rain-shadow streak, and a lumpy cauliflower ring. Shading HAS improved since the all-white cycle 1, but the cap undersides are now near-black ((50,53,58) at 8 s), which is too dark for a water cloud under a 39 deg sun.
issues.fix: Column noise: in stem_density stretch the noise vertically (stem_col.w about 3.5) and cut the amplitude from r*0.6 to r*0.25 for streaky straight walls. Add crown spikes above 0.85*h (thresholded high-frequency nbl). col_waist -0.1 -> 0.0, col_flare 1.2 -> 1.05. Column tint [0.80,0.80,0.78] with grey-brown sediment streaks. Cap: cap_aspect 0.55 -> 0.42, head_noise_amp 0.4 -> 0.6, billow_sharp 1.3. Soften macro_s and raise the multiple-scattering floor (systemic).

issues.problem: The base-surge timing and radius are now right (FIXED: visible from 15 s, about 920 m at 30 s), but its shape is a hard mesa. At 15 s a trapezoid 'plinth' with straight sloped sides, a flat top and grainy dither sits around the column base. At 30 s and 60 s it is a flat-topped table with vertical square ends. Early on it is too tall (surge_h0 270 m vs 130 m at 10 s). The real surge is a brilliant white, rolling, billowing front that is tallest at the front, with a clear centre after about 1 min.
issues.fix: surge_h0 270 -> 130. For column kinds, give sdf_skirt a front-loaded profile: prof = 0.35 + 0.65*smoothstep(0.5, 0.95, x)*(1 - smoothstep(0.95, 1.15, x)), with a rounded torus head at the front. Add height noise of amplitude 0.5h at cell size 0.15R in skirt_density, and ramp surge_inner to 0.55 by 60 s.

issues.problem: The cap floats as a perfect cumulus egg for 4 minutes with no rain-out, no dark slate-grey hanging lobes and no rain curtains; the column just fades away cleanly. The dossier says the outer shell collapses in lobes from 12 s, rain reaches the sea at about 1 min, and the head is gone by 2.5 min. The surge never lifts into the grey stratocumulus deck (from about 210 s).
issues.fix: Set cap_fade about 80 (density reaches 0 by 150 s). From col_fall = 14 s, add rain-curtain density below the head (vertical streak noise, albedo [0.45,0.48,0.50]) and darken the collapsing column. After 210 s, raise the surge base (skirt_state bottom offset rising to 460 m at 270 s).

issues.problem: Shock-shell refraction hairline arcs still cross the cloud and sky (REMAINS): a thin grey circular arc runs from (150,730) over the top to (1450,730) at 0.6 s, with more arcs at 0.2, 1.2 and 2 s. Cause: in shockwave.gdshader, rim pow(graze,16) is drawn with alpha rim*0.9 and refraction offset 0.006.
issues.fix: Use pure refraction: a = 0 for the rim and only the bg offset, offset 0.006 -> 0.0015. For NUCLEAR_UNDERWATER scale strength by 0.2 and hide the shell where it is inside the volume's alpha (draw it before the volume, or skip pixels where the volume depth is nearer).

issues.problem: The noon sky is a dull desaturated grey-teal ((110,138,147)) with no clouds. The references show a bright tropical sky with trade-wind cumulus, and the residual Wilson sheet at cumulus base is part of the look.
issues.fix: Use a humid noon preset with a bluer zenith, plus a scattered cumulus layer at 600-900 m that the remnant Wilson sheet can sit on.

issues.problem: Salt-and-pepper dither grain is visible in the surge and at the column base (white-noise hash12 dither, single frame).
issues.fix: Use blue-noise or IGN dither, and 2x base_steps in movie/offline mode.

issues.problem: WORSE than cycle 1. At 5 s a ~1.9 km wide black vase or 'flag' with horizontally brushed edges fills the frame. Its width is col_radius 420 x col_spread x (1 + col_cone 1.2), with col_flare 2.0 at the base, while the column is only ~750 m tall. From 8 s it becomes a straight-sided chimney or silo with a smooth helmet lid (col_cap_r 450, cap_aspect 0.5) and vertical waterfall streaks. It reaches ~2.8 km by 15 s and 3.5 km by 30 s because col_rise is still 28 s. The dossier gives a ~300 m spiky bush, a ~610 m ejecta apex at 12-15 s, and a lumpy cauliflower dust tower reaching 3.7 km only at 5-6 min. This reads as a jellyfish or factory smoke stack, not ref 01.
issues.fix: bomb_profiles sedan: col_rise 28 -> 120 (or two phases: ejecta to 600 m by 12 s, then a buoyant tower with tau ~100 s), col_cone 1.2 -> 0.25, col_flare 2.0 -> 1.3. In _column_stem multiply r by lerp(0.3, 1.0, smoothstep(col_delay, col_delay + 40, t)) so the column is ~130 m at 3.5 s and 420 m at ~60 s. Remove the smooth lid: cap_aspect 0.5 -> 0.9, head_noise_scale 0.9 -> 0.3, head_noise_amp 0.5 -> 0.8, billow_sharp ~1.2, so the top is billows merging into the column. Fade the jet/crown branch of stem_density after ~15 s (pass a 'jet' strength uniform = 1 - smoothstep(10, 25, age)), so the late column is cauliflower and not vertical jets.

issues.problem: PARTLY FIXED: at rec_km 12 the dome is now on screen, but it renders as a low flat-topped mesa (table mountain). It is ~450 m wide and only ~20 m tall, with straight sides and a flat top. The g_dome Gaussian is r 115 m, h 87 m at 2.5 s, which should give a rounded ~230 m x 87 m swelling. The camera-centred terrain LOD undersamples g_dome at 12 km, so vertices miss the peak. There are no radial cracks, no dust streaming from the cracks, and no 0.24 s spall dust haze. The 0.5-2.5 s frames are effectively empty desert.
issues.fix: Do not rely on terrain vertex displacement. Either add an opaque soil SDF dome to explosion_volume.gdshader (spherical cap radius dome_r, height from dome_state, ground_col albedo, radial crack noise with thin dust wisps where cracks open after ~2 s), or spawn a dedicated high-res displaced patch at GZ (>=128x128 vertices over 400 m) for 0-4 s. Add a spall haze: a skirt pulse at 0.24 s with radius ~500 m, height 10-20 m, density 0.3, tan, fading by 3 s.

issues.problem: The venting does not match refs 02/03, which show a spiky dark bush with salmon-peach glow leaking through cracks. Instead there are three separate CG elements. (1) A smooth orange 'flocked' ellipsoid (_hidden_fireball at 3050-2440 K, which reads saturated orange, not dull salmon) sits on the mesa. (2) A semi-transparent dark-brown mushroom head floats above it at 3.2 s, with two orange glow 'eyes' left and right (_column_head heat_glow torus cross-section). (3) A band of black/grey CG cubes (DebrisLayer boxes, debris_size 3, dark debris_color) is piled around the base like coal lumps. The exposure also dips (see below).
issues.fix: _hidden_fireball: temp lerp 3200->1400 -> 2100->1200, vent_radius 70 -> 45, and mask opacity with high-frequency crack noise so it only shows between dark jets. col_delay 3.0 -> 3.4, and keep _column_head density 0 until ~8 s (no head during venting). Set heat_glow of the column head to 0 for sedan (delete the 'eyes'). Debris: drop the cube look (see streamers): debris_count 5000 -> ~150, debris_size 3 -> 12-20 m, elongated along velocity, with cream dust trails.

issues.problem: REMAINS. The defining Sedan image (ref 01) is missing: dozens of cream-white ballistic streamers (clods trailing dust) arcing out and down like a palm crown, landing out to ~1.7 km with small puffs. Only vertical jet streaks inside the column and the black cubes are present.
issues.fix: Implement a streamer mode in DebrisLayer/debris.gdshader: ~80-150 clods launched at 100-140 m/s in a 55 deg cone, each leaving a ribbon or billboard trail of colour [0.80,0.75,0.65] whose width grows with age and fades over ~15 s, plus a ground puff on impact. Alternatively, add N parabolic tube SDFs to the volume shader for 4-20 s.

issues.problem: The palette is FIXED: the column is now grey-brown and darker than the ground, and the surge is beige. But it is overcorrected. The shadow side of the column is pure black (RGB ~25-35), and a straight vertical terminator splits the column into black and tan halves, so it reads as a lit CG cylinder. In ref 01 the shadow side is slate grey-blue at roughly 100-120. Causes in explosion_volume: macro_s = dot*0.55+0.5 reaches ~0; ao only probes upward (od_up through km of column gives ao 0.15); and the multiple-scatter floor is only 0.05.
issues.fix: explosion_volume.gdshader: macro_s -> clamp(dot(...)*0.4 + 0.6, 0, 1); for stems, add a sideways ao probe (p + vec3(nr.x,0,nr.y)*stem.z*0.6) and floor ao at ~0.35; raise the multiple-scatter term 0.05 -> ~0.12 scaled by albedo. Verify that the column's shadow side is ~0.35-0.45 of its sunlit side.

issues.problem: A dark vertical seam runs down the exact centre of the column, the vent ball and the head (clearly visible at 3.6, 5, 8, 15 and 60 s). Thin straight 'antenna' spikes and ray-like sticks radiate from the column top (5-240 s). The jet noise in stem_density uses nbl(vec3(ang*2.2 + seed, ...)) with ang = atan(p.z, p.x), which is discontinuous at +/-pi; the half-plane seen edge-on becomes a vertical line. The jets also extend above stem.y as rigid spikes.
issues.fix: Make the jet lookup periodic: jet = nbl(vec3(cos(ang)*1.4, sin(ang)*1.4, h01*0.9) + seed)*0.7 + nbl(vec3(cos(ang)*3.3, sin(ang)*3.3, h01*2.3 + 1.7))*0.3. Clamp the jet term to zero above stem.y - r and soften with the existing top fade. The same code affects Tallboy and Grand Slam.

issues.problem: REMAINS. The surge still starts at 4 s (surge_start 4.0), so a >1 km beige skirt already exists at 8 s. The dossier gives fallback starting at 10-20 s, about 1 km at 40-60 s and 4 km at 4-6 min. From 30 s it is a flat-topped, uniform-height bread loaf with rounded ends and no lobes. The colour is now correct (beige-grey).
issues.fix: surge_start 4 -> 12, surge_tau 45 -> 150, surge_h0 150 -> 100. In skirt_density, raise the low-frequency lf amplitude (1.4 -> 2.5) at lower frequency so the front is lobed with varying height. Taper the height toward the front and add a few rising plumes.

issues.problem: REMAINS and WORSE. Sky and ground darken by ~0.85 stop (exp 0.42 -> 0.233; the log shows adapt 0.85, flash 0.8) because of an invisible buried vent. Cycle 1 measured ~0.5 stop.
issues.fix: explosion_profile.light_power: NUCLEAR_BURIED 0.03*opacity -> 0.002*opacity, or skip step_adaptation for buried/column kinds.

issues.problem: Full-width bright horizontal stripes cross the terrain (0.5-3.6 s). From 15 s a pale flat rectangular band sits in the foreground, and a dark diagonal line on the right reads as a texture seam. The near-horizon sky is slate grey at 0.5-2.5 s but deep blue later. There are no mountains, unlike refs 01 and 02.
issues.fix: Fix the terrain grazing-angle texture and LOD seams (anisotropic filtering, detail noise), add a distant ridge silhouette, and calibrate the horizon haze toward the pale blue of ref 01.

issues.problem: WORSE than cycle 1. At 0.5-1 s the ball is a dull grey-beige 'cotton' disc with brown blotches in a pitch-black frame (exp 0.0009, adapt 8.9-9.0 stops). At 2 s it is a brown spongy disc, and at 5 s a dim orange ball with a visible rectilinear lattice. It never reads as blinding or incandescent. Causes: (a) metered_luminance aims l_fb/(3*amb), about +1.5 EV, with max_comp up to 10 at full coverage, so the camera places the ball in the mid-tones; (b) the shader modulates temperature with tloc = T*mix(0.70, 1.18, fpatch), so cool cells are 0.7^4 = 1/4 as bright, giving dirty brown blotches; (c) the seamless-noise lattice (see systemic). RDS-37 at adapt 7.4 still reads white, which supports the metering diagnosis.
issues.fix: explosion.gd metered_luminance: l_fb divisor 3.0 -> ~16 (ball about +4 EV: the core clips to white and structure shows only in the highlights and limb), and max_comp lerp(6,10,cov) -> lerp(6,7.5,cov) for the zoom/eye view. explosion_volume emission: narrow the cell temperature spread while the ball is young, e.g. tloc = T*mix(1.0 - s, 1.0 + s*0.4, fpatch) with s = mix(0.08, 0.30, smoothstep(3*t2, 15*t2, age)) (pass via an fb_look/fb_shape slot). Target: white-yellow at 0.5-2 s, yellow at 5 s, orange by 8-10 s.

issues.stage: 8-90 s (incandescent torus under a brown cap)
issues.problem: REMAINS. At 10 s there is a uniform hairy orange sphere with no torus and no dark top. At 20-40 s there is a matte red-brown smooth 'potato' with no glow at all, floating above a detached grey haze. The King reference (XX-42 at ~1 min, and DOE film frames rows 3-4) shows a blazing orange-yellow underside or torus under a dark red-brown top, with a thin reddish stem. That is King's defining look, and it is entirely absent. The core glow sits deep inside an optically thick head (kh = 22/size) at the default core_glow 0.7, so none of it escapes.
issues.fix: ivy_king: core_glow 1.4, core_cool_s 40 -> 90, core_radius 0.35. In head_density change 'dens *= 1.0 - 0.75*hot' -> 0.95 so the hot ring is optically thin, and move the glow ring toward the underside (glow distance computed from rc + vec2(0, H*0.25)). In head_state make torus reach 1 by ~20-30 s, not 0.07*t_stab. Use dark_base ~0.8 inverted (top darker than the glowing underside). Check at 20, 40 and 60 s that the underside glows orange-yellow against a brown top.

issues.problem: REMAINS and more visible. A thin translucent hoop like an angel's halo floats around the top of the cap from 40 to 180 s. The cause is ice_cap r_rel 1.1 (wider than the cap) built from a hollow sdf_shell (abs(e) - 0.07*s.z), so only the grazing limb shows. rings=1 is still set: at 40 s the ring disc cuts through the cap underside as a smeared white horizontal band, and at 90 s it is a detached Saturn ring around the stem. Neither is documented for King.
issues.fix: ivy_king: rings 1 -> 0. ice_cap dur 0.3 -> 0.07, r_rel 1.1 -> 0.8, lift 0.1 -> 0.0, opacity 0.7 -> 0.45. In sdf_shell for the pileus, use a solid thin lens (max(e, -(q.y - s.z*0.2)) with density falloff) instead of a hollow shell, so it reads as a smooth cap hugging the dome top and disappears before ~60 s.

issues.problem: REMAINS. The stem is a white or blue-grey pillar 0.4-0.7 of the cap width: stem_color [0.72,0.70,0.68] and the default stem_r, about 0.7 of the cap at 90 s. At 20-40 s it is separated from the cap by a large gap. The reference shows a thin reddish-brown stem of ~0.15-0.2 of the cap width, attached to it.

issues.problem: REMAINS. The grey igloo is gone, but the documented bright condensation dome and discs (R ~1.2-2 km, 0.5-5 s, lighting the cloud deck yellow) are also gone, because fx_layers disables Wilson for w_kt > 150 unless wilson_force is set. issues.fix: ivy_king: wilson_force True, wilson_start 0.5, wilson_duration covering ~5 s, wilson_flatten 0.5. Render it bright and fireball-lit (see the systemic condensation lighting fix). issues.problem: Two things are FIXED: cap growth (cap_d_keys gives plausible width/height ratios of ~0.55 at 90-180 s) and the bunker roof clipping (the cap is on screen at 360 s). But the late cloud is a stock Hollywood mushroom. The dome is perfectly smooth grey with no cauliflower and the underside is near black. issues.fix: Head noise cell from H (see systemic), head_noise_amp 0.3 -> 0.5, whiten_time 0.5 -> 0.8. Add a flat anvil skirt at ~18 km with a small overshoot dome (overshoot ~0.05 with a flattened top). Use wind shear increasing to ~10-20 m/s at wind_h ~15 km. Fix the underside lighting (systemic).

issues.problem: PARTLY IMPROVED. The sky is still black at 10 s (adapt 2.95) and dark teal at 20 s (adapt 0.55), although 90% of the thermal energy is out by ~8 s, so the ball floats in a void.

issues.problem: The limb has a ragged dandelion-like fur of tiny flame wisps (fireball_noise 0.22 plus the n2 octave and a soft edge), so the ball looks hairy rather than shock-bounded and crisp.
issues.fix: For t < t_fb_max, scale the fireball displacement amplitude by ~0.35 and sharpen the edge: smoothstep(0.05,-0.12,dd) -> smoothstep(0.015,-0.05,dd). Clamp the per-sample emission at the limb.

issues.problem: The ground-hugging hemisphere is FIXED, but its look is WORSE. At 0.5 s it is a grey-beige mottled sponge in a black frame (adapt 8.4). At 2 s it is brown 'burlap' with an obvious axis-aligned lattice (adapt 8.8), and at 5 s a dim brown-orange lattice dome. issues.problem: The brown cloud, dark stem and cap growth are FIXED. But the cap is a smooth orange-terracotta 'hamburger bun' at 40-180 s and a noise-free lens or flying saucer with a crisp rim and a nearly black underside at 360-600 s. issues.fix: Head noise cell from H, not max(R,H) (see systemic); head_noise_amp 0.3 -> 0.55; billow_sharp ~1.0; keep torus with roll visible to ~2 min. Colours: head_color_early [0.28,0.15,0.08] -> [0.26,0.18,0.12] (lower chroma), head_color_late [0.38,0.31,0.25] -> [0.36,0.33,0.30], whiten_time 2.0 -> 1.0. issues.fix: data/bombs.json b83 rec_km 55 -> ~30 (1 psi is at ~19 km). Set skirt_color [0.36,0.29,0.22], dust_color [0.45,0.37,0.28], skirt_height 1.8, and fade the skirt out by ~3 min. issues.problem: REMAINS (rings=1). At 40 s a white smeared horizontal band crosses the middle of the cap, because the ring at cloud_top*0.25 intersects the head volume. At 90 s a thin white streak ring crosses the stem. This is wrong for a dry desert surface burst and looks CG.
issues.fix: b83: rings 1 -> 0. In rings_state, never place a ring above head bottom minus one ring thickness.

issues.problem: The stem has a hard two-tone split: the upper third is near-black and the lower part grey-brown, divided by a crisp horizontal boundary. This comes from cheap_density's sharp head term (-sdf/(H*0.25)) casting a knife-edge shadow, combined with the upward-only ao.
issues.fix: cheap_density: head term divisor H*0.25 -> H*0.6 with one low-frequency noise tap. Apply the sideways ao floor for stems (systemic).

issues.problem: At 20 s there is a dim red-brown blob in a dark sky (adapt still 2.1 stops). There is no visible red-brown torus lifting off and no thick dark soil stem being pulled up while debris rains back (dossier: from 10 s).
issues.fix: Use the same exposure-recovery fix as King. Make the torus visible from ~10 s (torus ramp). Start the stem at t_fb_max*0.5 with density ramping over ~5 s and flare 2.6 so a dark column rises visibly into the ball between 10 and 30 s.

issues.problem: REMAINS. After 10 minutes the cloud is perfectly axisymmetric and vertical: wind [2.5,-1.5] m/s at wind_h 1000 m drifts the top by only ~1.7 km against a 35 km cap. There is no dark fallout curtain downwind.
issues.fix: Increase upper winds (10-25 m/s at 10-20 km with shear). Add a fallout curtain: a skirt/column offset downwind from ~5 min, dark grey-brown, density 0.3, falling streaks.

issues.problem: The cap touches and clips the top edge of the frame, because shot_rig's 'top' ignores the noise amplitude, overshoot and wind.
issues.fix: In shot_rig._setup_view_dynamic, add head_noise_amp*half to top and use size = max(top, 0.6*w)*1.45.

issues.problem: NEW and WORSE. tod_hist 'dawn' (sun at 1.6 deg elevation) produces an olive-green/khaki sky and a rust-red 'Mars' ground with noisy tiling and a hard horizontal texture seam (e.g. y~815 at 180 s). The haze is lavender. The shot looks like an alien planet. The documented scene is a solid grey two-layer overcast topping out at 10 km, low winter light at 09:47 local, a frozen feather-grass steppe, the flash lighting the overcast from below, and the cap punching through the deck within 1-2 min.

Add a 'winter overcast' preset in environment_ctl: sun elevation ~12 deg but direct sun_e ~0.3, a uniform grey sky (fog_col ~[0.62,0.63,0.65]), ambient-dominated light, and a pale straw/grey ground [0.55,0.52,0.45]. Add a cloud-deck layer at 8.5-10 km that the head SDF punches through, lit by g_fireball_color in the first 10 s. issues.problem: At 0.5 s the ball is acceptably blinding white. From 2 s it is a perfectly round cream, then peach, mottled ball (with the lattice) in a pitch-black frame (adapt 6.3-8.2). The flattened underside from the ground-reflected shock (2-4 s), the dusty Mach ring and the broad low billowing dust skirt are all absent. issues.fix: rds37: reflect_cut_t ~2.5 (fireball_cut_y flattens the bottom to ~0.72R). skirt 0.3 -> 0.9, skirt_color [0.50,0.43,0.35], skirt_height 1.5. Discs: in explosion_volume, raise the fireball illumination factor 0.25 -> ~1.0 for ring/shell media, raise ring density op*0.22 -> op*0.6, and make the discs thin (vertical scale 3 -> 6), white and bright yellow-lit, opacity <= 0.4. Apply the King metering fix.

issues.problem: REMAINS. From 40 s the cloud is a pale pink-grey smooth mushroom on a uniform pale grey tube (a 'PVC pipe' or tornado). It is the same grammar as King, just pinker. The signature 'thin dark twisting dust stem rising from the centre of a wide low dust base' is absent: stem_color [0.30,0.27,0.25] renders pale lavender-grey through the 60 km haze and dawn ambient, with no twist and no flared dusty foot.

issues.problem: REMAINS (the profile is unchanged: radius_m 9000, height_rel 0.45, dur 0.6). It renders as a flat translucent glass dish or contact lens 14-18 km wide with a hard elliptical rim. Its hollow interior shows the sky through it in mottled patches, and the stem pierces it. The dossier describes a translucent bell around mid-stem, about half the cap's width, at ~30-120 s.
issues.fix: tier2: radius_m 9000 -> ~3000, height_rel 0.45 -> 0.3, t_on 0.10 -> 0.06, dur 0.6 -> 0.2, opacity 0.45 -> 0.3. In sdf_shell for which=1, build an open-bottom bell (narrow at the stem at the top, flaring downward) with solid low density and noise-eroded edges, not abs(e) shells.

issues.problem: REMAINS. The third ring_list entry [40,160,6500,5200,200] is a detached hoop ~10 km wide around a stem 2.6 km wide, with a large gap: a Saturn ring. At 90 s ring material also cuts across the bottom of the cap as a bright smeared band.

issues.problem: At 20 s the cap is an orange-red glowing 'jelly bean' ellipsoid (the core-glow band is visible, which is good). At 40 s it is salmon pink, and from 90 s grey-pink. There is no red-brown cap with crimson glints and no dark top. It whitens far too early (whiten_time 0.4).
issues.fix: whiten_time 0.4 -> 0.8, head_color_early [0.36,0.14,0.07] -> [0.32,0.15,0.09], head_color_late -> grey-blue [0.70,0.72,0.76] per Sakharov. Keep core glow flickering at low strength to ~60 s (core_cool_s 45 -> 60).

issues.problem: The scene is still 3.7 stops down at 10 s and 1.5 stops down at 20 s. The flash is documented as over by 10-12 s.
issues.fix: Use the same fireball-only metering and faster recovery as for King.

issues.problem: The fireball looks like a beige sponge cake. Every frame from 0.1 s to 20 s is a hemisphere, later a sphere, covered in small blobs that are all the same size. Axis-aligned tile seams and mirrored repeats of the noise tile are visible across the ball: FxResources builds a 96^3 noise texture with get_seamless_image_3d (skirt 0.1), and the shader tiles it 2-5 times across the ball. A fine per-pixel grain sits on top. The limb is torn cotton with dark-brown smoky tendrils. The 20 s frame is a perfectly round orange sitting on the horizon, with no limb brightening or darkening. The references show something else: the high-speed frame has a crisp, smooth limb with a few LARGE patches, and IvyMike2 shows a brilliant smooth white dome ('sun half-risen').
issues.fix: Profile changes: fireball_noise 0.22 -> 0.05 (crisp limb), fireball_noise_scale 10 -> 3.5 (about 5-8 patches across the ball), mottle_t2 2.5 -> 5. In explosion_volume.gdshader fireball_density, change the edge smoothstep(0.05,-0.12,dd) to smoothstep(0.015,-0.04,dd). Take the patch and mottle terms from noise_a (simplex fBM), not the cellular billow texture. Rotate each octave's lookup by a fixed non-axis-aligned mat3 so tile seams never line up. In FxResources, either make truly periodic noise (skirt 0) or raise SIZE to 128. In the albedo mix, multiply the c_fb term by fb_shape.w (skin) so the hot ball has no brown, lit, smoke-like fringe.

issues.problem: The fireball and the cloud are still two separate primitives (REMAINS from cycle 1). At 40 s a textured glowing ball hangs under a smooth, translucent rust-coloured blob. At 90 s a salmon textured half-ball sticks out under a pink cap. At 180 s a blurry salmon-pink disc floats in the sky gap under the cap. There are three causes. (1) fireball_state uses head_center_y() (the tanh rise, about 5.8 km at 40 s), while head_state switches to top_keys after t_fb_max (about 7.7 km). (2) t_fb_max = 10*t2 = 24 s for 10.4 Mt, so the fireball opacity fade window of 4-12 t_fb_max runs from 98 s to 293 s. (3) Head density only ramps in over 10-40 t2 (24-98 s). The fireball_temperature tail (about 3000 K at 40 s, about 1300 K at 180 s) also keeps head_heat glowing, because tc = max(tt, core_t).
issues.fix: (a) In fireball_state, set center_y to the same value head_state returns: add a shared head_center_eff(t) that applies top_keys. (b) Add art keys fb_fade_s=[15,45] for Mike, used in place of smoothstep(4,12 t_fb_max), and head_appear_s=[6,25] used in place of (t/t2-10)/30. (c) In head_state, use tc = max(tt*(1-smoothstep(fb_fade_s)), core_t) and set core_cool_s 80 -> 45, so the cap glow lives only in the torus core and is gone by about 90 s.

issues.problem: The stem is detached from the cap. A flat-topped pale column stops 2-4 km below the cap and open sky shows between them: a mushroom on a separate pole (WORSE than cycle 1). In stem_state, top = min(head_bottom+0.45*half, rising), and 'rising' climbs at 0.75*avg_speed, so it lags the top_keys-driven head. The 0.3R under-cut hollow in sdf_head_base and the stem-top density fade over 1.5 radii widen the gap further.
issues.fix: In stem_state, for attached stems, once t > t_start + 10 s set top = hs.center_y so the top fade happens inside the cap. Also clamp it to at least head_bottom - 0.1*half. Reduce the under-cut radius in sdf_head_base from R*0.30 to R*0.18. Join stem and head with smin(.., .., H*0.3) in scene_sdf and in cheap_density.

issues.problem: Mike's key colour contrast is missing. The stem is pale peach-white, the same tone as the cap, where IvyMike2 shows a dark red-brown dirty stem under a white cap. The cycle-1 fix was not applied: stem_color is still [0.50,0.45,0.40]. The base is a flat white band, either running across the whole horizon (40 s) or a thin puck (90-600 s). The required water curtain rising around the base at 10-90 s does not exist.
issues.fix: Set stem_color to [0.26,0.19,0.13] and stem_density 1.1 -> 1.6. In explosion_volume, scale the ambient term by albedo (amb*ao*0.6 -> amb*ao*0.35) so dark media stay dark. Add curtain art keys in skirt_state, curtain_h=1500 m, curtain_t=[10,90]: a ring wall at about 0.7*skirt radius that rises by 25 s and collapses by 90 s. Give it a ragged rounded top, not a slab.

issues.problem: The cap has no Mike character. At 40 s it is a smooth matte rust blob. At 90 s it is a pink macaron with horizontal ring stripes across it. In macro_h, perturb the normal with cauli: dot(nrm,L) + 0.35*(cauli-0.5), so the terminator breaks along the billows. Set whiten_time 0.4 -> 0.12. After 300 s, lower cap_aspect_max to about 0.35 for a flat anvil top. Add a small turret ellipsoid (about 6 km wide, up to 41 km) from 360 s.

issues.problem: The condensation features look CG. rings=3 renders as thin wire 'orbit-line' ellipses around the cap and stem (40 s and 90 s) and a faint arc at 360 s. The ice cap is a hollow halo outline above the head at 40 s and a fluffy, greenish sombrero brim around the top at 90-180 s. It is visible from 31 s to 380 s (dur 0.4*t_stab). The reference shows smooth laminar pileus sheets cutting across the stem at 2.5-6 min, and no hat brim.

For ice_cap use t_on 0.05 -> 0.08, dur 0.4 -> 0.12, r_rel 1.1 -> 1.0 and lift 0.1 -> 0.2. Render it as a filled thin lens, not the hollow sdf_shell.

issues.problem: The fireball floats in a black void. From 0.1 s to 20 s the sky and the sea or ground are RGB 0, even after a +4 EV shadow lift (adaptation 8.5-9 stops). There is no atmospheric glow around the ball, no trade-cumulus deck lit orange below it (the main look of IvyMike2), no light on the surface, no five lightning channels at 5-80 ms, and no Wilson flash at 1-5 s.

Add 4-6 emissive jagged line meshes at about 1 km radius, 5-80 ms. Set wilson_force=True, wilson_start=1.0, wilson_duration=0.3 with a bright translucent look.

explosion_profile.gd _column_head couples head size and height to the CURRENT collapsing column. Radius = cap*(0.35+0.65*grow), where grow = h/hmax uses the post-col_fall h, and center_y uses h unless cap_hold_peak. So every column-path bomb's cloud shrinks and/or sinks when col_fall starts: Mk 82 r about 13->8 m (1->4 s), Mk 84 25.7->15.4 m (2->4 s), Tallboy center about 175->68 m (5->8 s), Grand Slam about 210->100 m (5->15 s). The auto-framing then jumps (Tallboy zooms in at 8 s). Fix once: base grow and h_ref on the peak column height (column height without the fall factor, or a running max), and enable cap_hold_peak for all buried kinds.

explosion_volume.gdshader stem_density, the crown/jet term: the noise uses only (angle, h01). Viewed side-on, the radial streaks become horizontal brush strokes and stacked bands (Mk 82/84 wings, the Tallboy/Grand Slam collapsed-column layers). atan(p.z,p.x) fed to non-periodic noise produces a vertical seam line on the axis in all four bombs. The sdf_stem cap plane (dv) and the y-fade smoothstep(stem.y + r*0.3, ...) cut all jets at one height, giving flat-topped frustums. Fix: periodic coordinates (cos/sin of the angle), a radial term (rxz/r), per-jet top heights, sparse coverage with gaps, and an outward jet tilt.

Column bombs are frozen between about 1 s and 5 s. The 'churn' uniform is churn/max(t_stab,10), and t_stab for an HE charge is long, so the noise moves about 0.03 cells/s. column_height saturates by col_rise. For conventional and column kinds pass absolute churn (about 4-8 cells/s), and keep geometry evolving (jet tops descending, curtain, spreading surge).

Late heads are rigid analytic ellipsoids. The wind shear p.xz -= wind*age*pow(p.y/wind_h,1.7) is applied inside compact puffs, which tilts them into rugby balls and streaks the noise into 'hair'. Macro shading from the analytic ellipsoid normal gives a straight Lambert terminator (half black, half cream). Fix: rigid head translation evaluated at head.y, shear only for stem and skirt, a macro normal from the cheap_density gradient, and a multiple-scattering floor of about 0.2-0.25 scaled by albedo.

Conventional fireballs render as pastel peach cotton wool with no incandescent core, bloom or glare. Cause: emission 220 x bb_lum(3300 K) about 0.03, so the radiance is only a few units, AgX bleaches it, and fireball_noise_scale 3 gives fine mottling. The crown (col_delay 0.02-0.03 at density 1.3) swallows the ball by 0.15 s. The exposure dip lags the flash: its minimum is at 0.15-0.4 s, not in the first frames. Raise emission 3-4x, use larger flame lobes, delay and ramp the crown, add asymmetric soot from life 0.1.

DustWallLayer (an open cylinder, min height 3 m x (1+p/10)) draws a translucent glass slab with hard vertical silhouette edges under every HE ground burst at 0.005-0.06 s. sdf_skirt's rim profile (peak at 0.9R, falloff over 0.9-1.12R) gives loaf or cake skirts with steep ends. _base_surge's 0.1 density floor keeps flat ground sheets to 60 s. Fix: silhouette alpha fade, delayed start at 1.5 r_fb, a soft radial profile with height noise, and fade to zero.

Debris: BoxMesh cubes with drag 0.12 1/s have terminal velocities of 55-160 m/s, so clods hang in the sky for 4-15 s and read as square pixels or confetti; under auto-zoom they become big boxes. Use drag about 0.6, a jittered rock mesh, 0.05-0.5 m sizes, launch azimuths tied to the crown jets, and ground-impact dust puffs for the fragment fans (Mk 82 to 150 m, Mk 84 to 250 m).

Ground events at the target are invisible at 2-5 km. g_dome (the camouflet heave) is a terrain-vertex Gaussian that the far terrain LOD cannot resolve. Craters show only as flat light mesas, and there is no spall ring. Framing and environment that cheapen every shot: the zoom auto-framing hides absolute scale (Mk 82 and Mk 84, and Tallboy and Grand Slam, fill the frame identically) and jumps when heads shrink (Tallboy 5->8 s, Grand Slam 0.3->0.6 s).
