The noon sky is a dull slate grey-blue with an INVERTED gradient (teal at the top, greyer and darker toward the horizon; a desert sky should whiten toward the horizon). Full-width bright horizontal terrain stripes and brushed ground texture remain in every frame (cycle 1). Overall contrast is low and hazy compared with the reference photos.

NOISE LATTICE (severity 3, every nuclear fireball 0.5-10 s): fireballs show an axis-aligned rectilinear grid that looks like woven burlap (B83 2 s and 5 s, King 1-5 s, RDS-37 2-10 s). FxResources._make builds the 96^3 textures with FastNoiseLite.get_seamless_image_3d(..., skirt 0.1). Godot's seam blending leaves low-contrast, doubled-feature bands at every tile boundary. fireball_density samples world-axis-aligned q*1.8 at four scales (x0.9, x1, x2.3, x2.6), giving ~3-9 seams per diameter at each scale, which superimpose into a grid. Fix: generate truly periodic noise (periodic Worley with wrapped feature points and periodic simplex, in GDScript or a compute shader); at minimum apply a fixed non-axis rotation matrix and incommensurate offsets to every nlf/nbl octave, raise SIZE to 128 and skirt to 0.25. Verify with a debug slice render.

FIREBALL METERING OVERSHOOT (severity 3): Explosion.metered_luminance targets l_fb/(3*amb) with max_comp up to 10. A ball that fills the binocular view is pushed into the mid-tones, so megaton fireballs at 0.5-5 s render as grey-beige or brown cotton in a pitch-black frame. The 6.3 'blinding white ball' signature of King, B83 and RDS-37 is lost, and this is WORSE than the clipped disc of cycle 1. Use a divisor of ~16 (about +4 EV), max_comp <= 7.5 in zoom, metering only while temp > 3000 K, and recovery tau ~1.5-2 s afterwards. Also reduce the early cell temperature spread mix(0.70,1.18) to about +/-8% while age < 3*t2: with x^4 luminance the current spread turns the cooler cells brown.

VOLUME SHADOWS TOO BLACK (severity 2, new overcorrection): after the albedo/ambient fixes, the shadow sides of columns and stems and the undersides of caps are near pure black (Sedan column, B83 cap underside at 360-600 s, King at 360 s). In explosion_volume: macro_s = dot*0.55+0.5 bottoms out at 0; ao only probes upward (ao = 0.15 under any thick cloud); the ground-bounce term is multiplied by (1 - hgt), so caps at altitude get none; the multiple-scatter floor is 0.05. Fixes: macro floor ~0.4-0.6; a sideways ao probe for stems with an ao floor of ~0.35; ground bounce weighted by clamp(-nrm.y,0,1) independent of altitude (cap undersides are lit by the sunlit desert); multiple scatter ~0.12*albedo.

CONDENSATION PRIMITIVES STILL CG (severity 2): the pileus is a hollow abs(e) shell wider than the cap (r_rel 1.1), so only its limb shows, as an angel's halo (King 40-180 s). Rings are detached hoops (King 90 s, RDS-37 180 s) and intersect the cap as smeared white bands (King 40 s, B83 40 s, RDS-37 90 s). tier2 is a glass dish (RDS-37). Use solid low-density lenses and collars with noisy edges, never place a ring inside or touching the head, and give the bell an open-bottom shape. Ring and shell media also receive only 0.25x the fireball light, so early condensation renders as dark smudges (RDS-37 5-10 s): use ~1.0.

WILSON GATE DELETES DOCUMENTED FEATURES (severity 2): fx_layers disables Wilson for w_kt > 150 without wilson_force. As a result, King (dome and discs 0.5-5 s) and RDS-37 (dome and discs 0.5-6 s) have no bright condensation at all. Add wilson_force for both, with a bright, flattened, fireball-lit look.

LARGE CAPS ARE NOISE-FREE (severity 2): head_density uses cell = max(R,H)*head_noise_scale and amp = head_detail.x*min(R,1.4H). On 10-35 km caps this gives smooth potato, bun and UFO silhouettes with crisp rims and no cauliflower (B83 360-600 s, King 180-360 s, RDS-37 360-600 s). Base the noise cell on H (about 0.3-0.4*H), add a fine octave, raise amp for megatons and add the torus roll that is still invisible.

STEM JET ANGLE SEAM (severity 2, column kinds): stem_density's jet noise uses atan(p.z,p.x)*2.2 as a coordinate, which is discontinuous at +/-pi. A dark vertical seam runs down the centre of Sedan's column, and the same code paths serve Tallboy and Grand Slam. Use periodic (cos(ang), sin(ang)) coordinates, and clamp the jets above stem.y, where they render as straight spike rays.

FIXED: the Wilson glass-dome hemispheres; DC's black bunker bar; unbounded skirt growth (now min(t-t_hit,40) plus a fade); over-lit white dust (skirts now match the ground colour); B61's 10-s peach glow and its stem joining the cap (now detached); B61's NO2 colour and the 0.02 s white-out; DC's 20-s salmon glow (core_cool_s); FOAB's flame-smoke snowman and its pastel-paper flame; MOAB's flame duration (fb_duration_s 2.4). REMAIN: conventional exposure stop-down; FOAB's missing FAE phases; skirt slab/puck shapes; dust bands; flat-topped stems; cap streaks. WORSE: MOAB's cloud (now pitch black, floating, nuclear mushroom), B61's late-cap swirl and brush streaks, and DC's cap colour (rust albedo replacing the glow).

CONVENTIONAL EXPOSURE (sev 3, MOAB/FOAB): Explosion.metered_luminance still applies the cov/l_fb fireball stop-down to conventional bursts (max_comp=4.0, adapt ~2 stops). The noon sky goes to charcoal or black at 0.2-7 s, and the flames render matte orange; brightened 3x offline they match the references. Fix: if prof.conventional, use lum = ill/amb only, set max_comp <= 1 and recovery tau ~1 s.

WIND SHEAR IMPLEMENTATION (sev 2-3, DC/B61/MOAB): explosion_volume.gdshader shifts each sample by p.xz -= wind*age*pow(clamp(y/wind_h,0,1.5),1.7). (a) The proxy box in Explosion._update_volume extends by only wind_v*t*1.5, while the shift reaches 1.99x, so drifted caps are clipped by a hard vertical wall (DC at 360 s). (b) Shearing the noise domain across the cap's height, with a clamp kink inside the cap, turns the cap texture into horizontal brush strokes, swirls and a thin halo line (B61 at 180-360 s, DC at 360 s, MOAB at 60 s). (c) Stems become smooth parabolic candy-canes. Fix: drift the head rigidly (drift evaluated at head.y), shear only the stem with per-height noise jitter, and set the box drift factor to >= 2.05 plus a radius margin.

HEAD SWALLOWS THE FIREBALL (sev 2-3): the cloud-head primitive appears early with r_now >= 1.04-1.05*r_fb, as an opaque, non-emissive shell. It hides DC's incandescence by 0.5 s, buries FOAB's flame by 3 s, and for MOAB it pops up above the flame as a separate ball. The head should grow out of the fireball: keep its radius below ~0.85*r_fb while the fireball opacity is > 0.3, reduce its density where it overlaps the flame, and delay conventional/thermobaric head appearance to ~0.45-0.6*dur.

STEM LAG AND FLAT TOPS (sev 2): stem_state's 'rising' term ((t-t_start)*avg_speed*stem_speed_rel) lags the head, leaving a floating cap above a flat-topped chimney (DC at 10-40 s, MOAB at 4-30 s). Only B61 should be detached. The 1.5-radius top fade in stem_density still reads as a cut pipe or 'tin can' (B61 column, MOAB, DC). Fix: for non-detached bombs, snap the top to head_bottom+0.45*half after ~2 s; fade over 3-4 radii with noise-modulated height and add a puff at the top of dust columns.

DUSTWALL LAYER (sev 2, all four bombs): the open-cylinder DustWallLayer draws (a) a hard-edged grey puck or glass slab under or inside the fireball at 0.005-0.5 s, because it is not hidden inside the fireball radius; and (b) a uniform band across the full frame width at 1-15 s, because op starts at 0.3 psi, height grows with r*0.035 and nothing fades it after the front passes. It never reads as a ring racing outward. Fix: multiply op by smoothstep(1.3,1.8,r/r_fb), raise the threshold to ~1 psi, cap height per yield, fade with exp(-(t-t_arr)/tau), and in dust_wall.gdshader fade alpha at grazing silhouettes (multiply a by smoothstep(0.05,0.35,abs(dot(nrm,view)))) so the cylinder ends are not hard vertical edges.

HEAD MORPHOLOGY IS A 'POM-POM' (sev 2-3): every cap (DC, B61, MOAB at 4-15 s) is a near-spherical felt ball with uniform fine fuzz. There are no large cauliflower lobes, no deep crevice shadows and no evolving silhouette. The b1 octave (nbl(np*0.32), about 1.7R) is too large to make lobes, and b3 adds fur. Fix: weight the lobe-scale octave (~0.3-0.4R) more, sharpen the billows (billow_sharp 1.4-1.8), drop the b3 weight, strengthen the od_local self-shadow, and add age-driven churn so lobes visibly boil.

LIGHTING OVER-CORRECTED (sev 2): shadow sides now crush to near black (B61 at 10 s: (23,22,24) against (176,126,89) lit; B61 at 180-360 s: black underside; FOAB: 17-24 grey everywhere). The cap's cheap_density shadow on the stem is a knife-edge horizontal step (FOAB 60 s: 24 -> 57 within 20 px). Fix: amb*ao*0.6 -> ~0.9 with an ao floor of 0.35, ground bounce 0.18 -> ~0.35, an albedo-scaled multiple-scattering term, and softer cheap_density falloffs (head /(H*0.8), skirt /(h*1.2)).

SIGNATURE COLLISIONS (sev 2, section 6.3): MOAB at 60 s and FOAB at 60 s are the same dark cap on a thick stem over a flat mound. DC and B61 are both rust-orange felt balls at 2-40 s. Fixing MOAB to a white, stemless thermal and DC to a white cap on a wavy stem would separate all four: MOAB white and stemless, DC a white column, FOAB a black smoke ball, B61 a red-brown detached ball.

SHOCK RIM (sev 1): shockwave.gdshader's rim term (pow(graze,16), alpha 0.9*strength) draws thin pen-line arcs and hemisphere outlines (FOAB at 0.05-0.5 s, MOAB at 0.4 s, DC at 0.1 s, B61 at 0.5 s). At 8-12 km a 0.01-0.3 kt shock front is a refraction shimmer, not a line. Fix: scale strength by the front's angular thickness (or ~0.2x for conventional and sub-kt bursts), and drop the alpha rim in favour of pure refraction offset.

ENVIRONMENT (sev 1-2): DC is rendered at dawn although Little Feller I fired at 10:00 PDT (set tod_hist to 'noon'). The dawn sky gradient goes olive-green overhead ((135,135,94)). The recovered noon sky is teal-grey ((113,129,133)) rather than desert blue. Long white horizontal stripes cross the terrain in every zoom frame, and a hard foreground seam with an orange speckled band appears at the bottom of DC's 90-360 s frames.

DEBRIS (sev 1): dark cubes show as uniform pepper specks around the ball (DC at 1-5 s, MOAB at 2-4 s). Use fewer and smaller visible pieces with a wide size distribution, quick fall-out and dust trails.

EXPOSURE (sev 3, IMPROVED but REMAINS): all three fireball bombs give pure-black sky and ground at 0.5-2 s. Logs: adapt 7.85 stops (Grable), 6.38 (Little Boy), 8.48 (Trinity) at 0.5 s; maxc 7.0-10.0. Recovery is now faster (tau 2.2 s; sky back by 5-10 s, cycle 1 needed about 20 s). Root cause: the zoom auto-frame (shot_rig._setup_view_dynamic) fills the view with the ball, so in Explosion.metered_luminance cov -> 1, max_comp = lerp(6,10,cov) and the meter keys on l_fb. Fix: nuclear max_comp = lerp(4.5, 6.0, cov), clamp cov to 0.35 (auto-zoom is not the eye being filled), weight l_fb by smoothstep(3000, 6000, T), and keep the sky at 40/255 or more once t > 3*t2.

HUMIDITY GATE DISABLES CONDENSATION SIGNATURES (sev 3, new root cause): shot_rig sets the global Game.humidity = 0.35, so WilsonLayer.amount = clamp((h-0.45)/0.35) = 0 for every bomb. This removes Baker's Wilson hemisphere (wilson 1.6 + wilson_force) and Little Boy's condensation shell. humid_site only changes cloud_top, and wilson_force only bypasses the >150 kt rule. Fix: a per-bomb site_humidity (Baker/Ivy/Bravo/Mike 0.85, Little Boy 0.8, Nevada sites 0.3) applied in main.prepare_world unless --humidity is passed. wilson.gdshader also needs a 'fill' mode; limb-only pow(1-facing,3) cannot make Baker's milky dome.

DAWN PRESET BROKEN AND MISAPPLIED (sev 3): environment_ctl DAWN (sun el 1.6 deg, orange sun, fog_col (0.42,0.38,0.40), exposure 1.5) renders an olive-green/khaki zenith (about (94,103,81)) and an orange 'Mars dune' foreground. It is used for Grable, whose dossier gives 08:29 with the sun 34 deg up and a blue sky, and for Trinity, which needs pre-dawn with the sun below the horizon, a blue-violet sky, a fireball-lit cloud deck and the cloud top in sunlight only at about 20 min. Fix: add ozone absorption to sky.gdshader scatter() (BETA_O about (0.65,1.88,0.085)e-6 /m with a density tent peaking at 25 km), make DAWN fog_col bluish, and add 'morning' and 'predawn' presets selected through tod_hist.

STEM:CAP PROPORTIONS ARE PHALLIC (sev 3, YouTube risk): in Grable, Little Boy and Trinity at 40-180 s the stem is 0.6-0.9 of the cap width, giving a 'tower plus knob' or 'i' silhouette. BlastPhysics.stem_radius = 0.5 x the FINAL cap radius, and stem_state reaches it at 0.4*t_stab while head_state reaches the full cap only at t_stab. Fix: stem radius = min(stem_r, 0.32*head_state(t).radius), stem_radius factor clamp(0.3 - 0.1*log10(W/20), 0.1, 0.3), stem_flare 1.7 or less.

CAP-STEM GAP AND 'BOX' STEMS (sev 2, REMAINS): in Grable, Little Boy and Trinity at 10-90 s the cap floats with empty sky under it, above a translucent, flat-topped, vertical-walled stem block with a hard vertical light/shadow split. Causes: stem_speed_rel 0.75 lags the head, the stem radius starts at 0.35*stem_r, the macro_s terminator is crisp, and the top fade is only 1.5 r. Fix: stem_speed_rel about 1.2, attach the top to head_bottom + 0.45*half after about 0.02*t_stab (dusty) or about 0.1*t_stab (air), narrow start radius for airbursts, macro_s = 0.35 + 0.65*smoothstep(-0.6, 0.8, ...), and a noisy top fade over about 3 r.

FIREBALL LOOK 0.5-5 s (sev 2-3, over-corrected since cycle 1): the clipped white disc became a dim 'crumpet/cork board' with uniform fixed-size Worley cells (fpatch drives tloc x0.70-1.18, about 8x luminance contrast), no limb darkening, a ragged fringe and a strong saturation push (pow(bc,1.7) at 0.55). It is orange at 1 s, a dark-red ember at 2 s and a matte maroon felt ball at 5 s, while the references show yellow-white at 1 s and a bright yellow-orange boiling cauliflower at 5-10 s (Trinity Aeby). The head_heat glow shows as a 'jack-o-lantern grin' band, not a bright torus ring. Fix: tloc mix(0.88,1.06), large nlf convective cells with a domain warp, limb darkening, saturation 0.25, fade_time 6-20 t_fb_max, and torus-rim emission instead of the density-reducing 'hot' term.

SPUN-SUGAR CAP STRIATIONS AND BLACK UNDERSIDES (sev 2): every late cap (Grable, Little Boy, Trinity at 90-360 s) shows concentric horizontal swirl streaks, like a wound ball of yarn or a lenticular cloud, and no cauliflower lobes. Cause: head_density rotates the noise domain by 'roll' (2.2 rad) scaled by smoothstep(0, a*0.8, rxz), which is a radius-dependent shear that smears the Worley cells into arcs. Undersides go near black (Little Boy (16,20,25), Baker (50,53,58)). Fix: roll 0.5-0.6 applied as a rigid rotation about the torus core (or only to the b3 octave), head_noise_amp 0.5, billow_sharp 1.3. Raise the multiple-scattering floor from 0.05 to about 0.2*albedo, and add ground bounce from below (ground_col*sun*L.y*0.35).

SHAPE GRAMMAR STILL SHARED (sev 3, section 6.3): the 90-360 s frames of Grable and Trinity are nearly interchangeable (same tower and knob, lean, olive sky and orange ground), and Little Boy has the same silhouette in grey. Little Boy's city layer is a uniform 'hedgerow' band. Fix: large-scale height noise (amplitude 0.5-1.5 h), front-loaded rolling-torus fronts for surges, rising plumes, and softer stem shadows on the skirt (cheap_density stem.z*0.4 -> stem.z*1.2).

ARTIFACTS STILL PRESENT: the screen-centre rectangular brightness seam (Grable 5 s, x=800 vertical step plus horizontal steps at y about 647 and 670) REMAINS. ROOT CAUSE FOR ALL MEGATONS: the time scales are keyed to t2 multiples that scale as W^0.44. With t_fb_max = 10*t2 we get 24/29/35/49 s for Mike/Bravo/219/Tsar. Head density only appears over 10-40 t2 (24-98 s for Mike, 49-195 s for Tsar). The fireball stays fully opaque until 4*t_fb_max (98-195 s) and fades out by 12*t_fb_max (5-10 min). On top of that, fireball_temperature's tail is still about 2900-3400 K at 40 s. Result: at 40 s the 219 and Tsar frames show a bare ball with no cloud, and Mike and Bravo show a glowing ball pasted under a thin cap. The dossiers say the ball reaches maximum size at 3-10 s, turns into a toroid by 20-40 s, and has no glow after 60-90 s. Fix in explosion_profile.gd: add art keys head_appear_s, fb_fade_s and t_fb_max_s (about 5-9 s for these four). Add the cycle-1 cool_k factor in fireball_state. In head_state, use tc = max(tt*fb_alive, core_t) so the fireball's tail cannot keep the cap glowing.

CENTRE MISMATCH: fireball_state.center_y uses head_center_y(t), the tanh rise, but head_state replaces center_y with top_keys - h after t_fb_max. The ball therefore hangs 1-3 km below the head in Mike and Bravo. Add one shared head_center_eff(t) and use it in fireball_state, head_state, stem_state, rings_state, ice_state, shot_rig framing and the light and exposure position.

FIREBALL TEXTURE (worst visual issue, 0.1-40 s on all four bombs, 8 of 13 frames each): fireball_density builds its displacement, mottle and patch terms from 96^3 FastNoiseLite get_seamless_image_3d textures. The blended skirt and the 2-5x tiling across the ball produce visible axis-aligned seam lines and mirrored repeats; the 219 20 s crop shows a clear grid. The cellular billow texture adds a uniform 'sponge/cottage-cheese' cell size, the large displacement (fireball_noise 0.22) gives a torn-cotton limb, and the brown c_fb albedo produces smoky dark fringes. Fix: non-axis-aligned rotated lookups per octave; truly periodic noise or no seamless skirt; mottle from the simplex fBM at 4-8 cells per diameter; displacement of at most 0.05; a sharp limb, smoothstep(0.015,-0.04); no albedo term while the ball is hot. Also blue-noise the dither, which currently shows as per-pixel grain.

BLACK VOID: from about 0.1 s to 20-40 s, sky and ground are exactly RGB 0 even after a +4 EV lift (adaptation 8.5-13.5 stops). In sky.gdshader the halo term (g_fireball_color.w*halo*0.02) is about 0.5% of the ball's radiance, and the terrain gets no reliable fireball light: the OmniLight has a 270-450 km range, a grazing angle and shadows on. Every reference (Tsar 1961, IvyMike2, all three Bravo) shows the ball wrapped in a big glow and the clouds, sea or ground lit. Fix: (1) Normalize the sky halo to the ball's radiance: about 0.2*exp(-(ang-ang_r)/(1.2*ang_r)) plus about 0.03*exp(-ang/0.3). (2) Add an analytic g_fireball inverse-square term with N·L to terrain.gdshader and water.gdshader. (3) Cap metered max_comp at about 8 stops in zoom (currently lerp(6,10,cov)). (4) Use a larger, low-threshold glow during the fireball phase.

CONDENSATION PRIMITIVES ARE CG: (a) sdf_rings is an anisotropic torus ((r-R)*0.3, (y-y0)*3) with density *0.22 and kr = 1/700, so rings read as thin wire 'orbit lines' or hoops with sky inside them. They should be opaque, flat, fireball-lit discs with no hole. (b) sdf_shell (abs(e)-0.07z) is hollow, so the ice cap and tier2 read as halo outlines, fluffy hat brims or glassy hula hoops; face-on optical depth is about 0.03, so stars show through them. (c) tier2 placement is wrong for every bomb: Bravo has a 60 km disc at 19.5 km instead of stem bells; Tsar and 219 have the wide tier under the cap instead of on top. (d) sd_ellipsoid and the scaled ring SDF are not true distances, so the empty-space skip leaps through thin sheets, giving holes and the rectangular seam beside Bravo's stem at 600 s. Fix: render the sheets as filled lenses; exclude rings and shells from the skip by forcing dt steps inside their y-slab (|p.y - y0| < 2*thickness); retime them per the dossiers.

STEM DETACHMENT (new): stem_state limits top to 'rising' = (t - t_start)*0.75*avg_speed, which lags the top_keys head. Combined with the 0.3R under-cut in sdf_head_base and the stem-top fade over 1.5 radii, this opens a 2-5 km sky gap with a flat-topped chimney (Mike 90/180 s, Tsar 90 s). For attached stems, run the stem into the head centre and smin the two together.

LATE CAP LOOK, identical on 17, 18, 19 and 20: a smooth ellipsoid 'flying saucer or hamburger bun' with blurry edges and a hard half-dark/half-lit vertical split from the squared macro term. head_heat on the torus shows as horizontal glowing stripes (Tsar 90 s), a salmon cotton-candy cap (90 s on all) or a pure-red band (219 at 180 s). There are no turrets, anvils, overshooting tops or virga. Fix: smaller noise cells (head_noise_scale about 0.22), a stronger billow amplitude and sharpness, a 4th octave, cauli-perturbed normals in macro_h, ambient scaled by albedo, glow attenuated by optical depth, and a flat anvil (cap_aspect_max about 0.35) after stabilization for Mike and Bravo.

ENVIRONMENT AND GRADING: every 'dawn' render (Mike, Bravo, Tsar) has a sickly olive-khaki-green sky gradient, where real dawn is a deep-blue zenith with an orange-pink horizon. The likely cause is linear RGB mixing of the blue scatter with the warm haze, then AgX. The ground is a saturated rust-red 'Mars' texture with a hard horizontal LOD or texture seam at about 85-90% of frame height (REMAINS). The per-bomb settings the dossiers depend on are unused: Mike's trade-cumulus deck at sunrise, Bravo's pre-dawn crimson twilight, Tsar's snow with overcast and a 2 deg golden sun. Without them 17, 18 and 20 are the same picture from 90 s on (section 6.3 violation).

FRAMING: _setup_view_dynamic sizes the view from the ground-zero distance. When the cap radius is comparable to the distance (Bravo 113 km at 100 km, Mike 61 km at 90 km), the cap's near edge is 40-60 km closer and rises off the top of the frame, so the 600 s anvil is cut off. Project the head's bounding box from the near edge (d - R) when choosing fov and aim. Auto-zoom also still removes absolute scale between ages; for the video, use a few fixed FOVs per bomb.

NIGHT RENDERING (219): stars show through translucent volume regions (the tier2 plate, cap underside edges). The 40-90 s frames are black because exposure stays adapted to a dim fireball the model keeps alive. No twilight band appears in frame. The stem, brightened by snow ground bounce, ends up brighter than the cap. Make volumes fully opaque where real density exists, stop metering on the fireball once its opacity falls below 0.3, and keep a minimum readable ambient on the cloud silhouette.
